meta.title: Awesome Agents That Learn
meta.subtitle: A research guide to self-learning, self-improving, and self-evolving AI agents.

papers.title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
papers.venue: Author reports NeurIPS 2026 PALM workshop; primary venue record not verified.
papers.code_note: An official implementation was not established in the inspected sources; no code or training was run.
papers.learning_signal: Memory-derived synthetic questions and a frozen base-model teacher conditioned on recent memory guide per-user adapter updates.
papers.mechanism: Distills session information into a persistent LoRA adapter using student-generated answers scored by a context-conditioned teacher. A verify-then-regenerate reader checks the adapter’s answer against a merged text store and uses the adapter-free model to regenerate unsupported answers.
papers.evaluation: Compares weight and text memory on 1,438 native HaluMem questions, delayed re-asks, and LoCoMo, with training-recipe, routing, and model-scale analyses.
papers.limitations: Recent-fact gains weaken as memories age. Routing improves overall accuracy but lowers the HaluMem conflict-category score. Refusal depends on synthetic unknown-answer training, and the paper identifies judge/rubric errors. Lower read-token use is not a complete cost result: writing is expensive and token accounting omits distillation compute.

papers.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
papers.code_note: Author project page inspected through public HTTP; an implementation release was not established. No code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Training-rollout contrasts and privileged training verifier information shape reusable guidance; online decisions use visible task progress.
papers.mechanism: Offline reflection learns a textual meta-skill about when to keep or change a harness. At deployment, a separate evolver uses that frozen guidance at checkpoints to edit notices, instructions, hooks, or tools. Each edit affects the current run; the next task starts from the seed harness.
papers.evaluation: Tests 60 held-out Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks with five runs each and 75 DeepSWE 1.1 tasks with three runs each. Includes component and checkpoint-frequency ablations and separate offline/online costs.
papers.limitations: Run-level contrasts do not isolate individual edits causally. Guidance is rebuilt for each benchmark/backbone, so the second-model result is not zero-shot transfer. Models, edit channels, checkpoint interface, and offline update procedure remain fixed; broader domain transfer and ongoing meta-skill learning are untested.

papers.title: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
papers.code_note: The manuscript promises code with its camera-ready version; a runnable release was not established. Nothing was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Visible development data and execution feedback guide research; hidden test scores are computed afterward.
papers.mechanism: Compares persistent sessions and workspaces with reset instances of the same research agent on matched task streams and time budgets. Separate first-solution, search-efficiency, and final-selection metrics distinguish reuse from better research outcomes. Insight-card interventions isolate explicit memory from session continuity.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates five native CLI agents across nine ML task families, typically with 30-minute budgets and three-to-five-task streams. Persistence improves aggregate search efficiency, but final-performance gains vary; stricter initialization controls remove the general search advantage.
papers.limitations: Four agents use one matched run pair per stream; one agent has three repeats. Cross-agent differences also include harness differences. The explicit-memory ablation covers one stream, and short related-task sequences do not establish long-term or open-ended scientific improvement.

papers.title: Can Benign Skills Induce Misaligned Behavior in LLM Agents?
papers.code_note: An official runnable artifact was not established in this review; no attacks or research code were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Successful benign traces and benign validation feedback build and refine skills; harmful-task outcomes are reserved for evaluation.
papers.mechanism: Compares fixed-model agents with and without reusable benign skills under matched requests and tools, then studies benign-feedback skill evolution, retrieval relevance, content ablations, and a pre-execution guard. Measures executed safety violations separately from completion of harmful objectives.
papers.evaluation: Studies five backbones on AgentHarm, LPS-Bench, and SafeAgentBench. Reports utility gains alongside increased unsafe-action rates, including violations in trajectories that never complete the harmful objective.
papers.limitations: Harmful requests are supplied at evaluation; this is not spontaneous misconduct during benign use. Unresolved trajectories without identified violations are excluded from unsafe-action rates. Some judgments use an LLM; content ablations also change length and wording. The guard terminates blocked runs, reduces benign utility, and leaves residual violations.

papers.title: Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment
papers.code_note: An official runnable artifact was not established in the inspected sources; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Game outcomes and traces drive the evaluated evolvers; independent game rules diagnose retained artifacts.
papers.mechanism: Tests artifact formation, behavioral change, useful action selection, preservation during composition, and extension across versions. Frozen-system interventions compare identical board states, complete games, and successive code versions rather than treating accumulated artifacts or higher scores as sufficient evidence of learning.
papers.evaluation: Studies Gomoku adaptations of Reflexion, Voyager, and DGM with one shared backbone, 1,876 fixed states, game traces, and a version lineage. Finds legality-only gains, conflicting skill composition, and later loss of previously passing states.
papers.limitations: These are study-specific adaptations in one rule-enumerable game, not replications of the original systems. Many diagnostic states come from DGM evolution games. Longer evolution, repeated training runs, other backbones, and open-ended transfer remain untested; the five-property definition is a proposed diagnostic framework.

papers.title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository and setup documentation inspected; contains adaptations of AHE and Meta-Harness, not an independently reproduced run.
papers.learning_signal: Task execution traces and benchmark outcomes drive harness edits; prior-task reevaluation measures retention.
papers.mechanism: Studies sequential evolution of Mini-SWE-Agent prompts, control flow, and tools with a fixed backbone. Adapted AHE and Meta-Harness optimize one task type and then another; manual trace analysis and edit ablations investigate verification, workflow, and budget conflicts.
papers.evaluation: Examines six source-to-target directions among sampled SWE-bench Verified, paraphrased SWT-Bench, and FeatureBench tasks. Reports severe earlier-task losses and analyzes 520 execution trajectories.
papers.limitations: Uses one backbone and reused subsets of 50, 50, and 30 tasks; no disjoint held-out evaluation is described. Scores are not full-benchmark results. These are study-specific implementations and pairwise transitions, not evidence that every harness or longer task sequence must forget.

papers.title: Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents
papers.code_note: An official implementation was not established in the inspected sources; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task outcomes update linear bandit estimates; trajectories and feedback drive language-model memory revisions.
papers.mechanism: Retains episodes and distilled guidance across tasks. A contextual bandit learns whether to solve directly, retrieve cases, retrieve guidance, or distill guidance before solving. Only the small routing models and external memories change; the backbone LLM stays frozen. An optional retry loop also reuses failures within a task.
papers.evaluation: Compares four backbones on BigCodeBench, SWE-bench Verified, MultiChallenge, and six BBEH tasks, separating first-attempt success from success within four attempts. Shared-memory and frozen-controller ablations examine routing.
papers.limitations: One run per benchmark/backbone; 100 BigCodeBench tuning tasks remain in its evaluation stream. Outcomes require test or judge feedback, and token accounting excludes evaluator calls. Gains vary by setting; the action space and learning procedure remain fixed.

papers.title: Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement
papers.code_note: An official implementation was not established in the inspected sources; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Incoming skill bodies, similar earlier skills, and body-derived synthetic queries guide metadata rewriting without evaluation labels.
papers.mechanism: Rewrites an incoming skill’s name and description to clarify supported capabilities and scope relative to nearby skills. The revised metadata persists in the growing library; earlier metadata, skill bodies, and router weights stay fixed.
papers.evaluation: Tests incremental versions of SRA-Bench, SkillRet, and SkillRouter across five routers, plus native Codex CLI skill selection. A separate 150-query, 87-skill check measures hidden-test task success.
papers.limitations: Main outcomes measure required-skill selection, not completed tasks. The principal stream deliberately adds confusable non-substitutes, using model judgments during construction. Random additions show smaller gains. End-task validation uses an early library and an added workflow prompt; it does not establish success at maximum library size.

papers.title: Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence
papers.code_note: The paper-linked LIFE repository returned HTTP 404 in two public retrieval checks. Implementation availability remains unverified; nothing was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Temporal labels train perception adapters; selected observations, task difficulty, and execution feedback support memory and tool construction.
papers.mechanism: Combines a separately trained streaming perception gate, evidence-preserving robot memory, and ReSight’s Explore–Distill–Mount process. Retained observations can acquire new indexes, and solutions can become reusable tools and skills. Runtime memory/tool updates are distinct from the gate’s offline LoRA training.
papers.evaluation: Tests perception and selective writing on streaming benchmarks, reuses ReSight capability-expansion experiments, and evaluates six questions three times each over one recorded day of robot video.
papers.limitations: The integrated study reconstructs memory offline; it does not test actions changing future observations. Capability-expansion results are inherited from ReSight, not independent new experiments. Answer-time savings exclude memory construction, and scoring/input protocols differ between configurations. Reliable multi-day autonomous learning remains open.

papers.title: Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime
papers.code_note: Paper-pinned snapshot c5c1963 and its README inspected. Current docs distinguish this earlier self-evolution experiment from the evolving hosting runtime; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Execution history, model cost, failures, and task feedback inform runtime code and policy revisions.
papers.mechanism: Allows an agent to edit its harness and improvement procedures while working. A separate mechanism retains history and controls activation; tools, context policies, and other edits can persist into later tasks without changing model weights.
papers.evaluation: Studies open-world game objectives, AppWorld scenario variants, SREGym incidents, and a coding-task sequence. Graded-task controls share the starting policy with editing disabled.
papers.limitations: Game results use one standalone/transfer pair per objective; low-reuse quests cost more. AppWorld/SREGym transfer stays within scenarios or fault families; coding has no separate holdout. The default guardian checks builds, not correctness, and the broadly writable development configuration does not enforce the paper’s protection assumptions.

papers.title: Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository inspected; simulator, robot models, and training code were not installed or run.
papers.learning_signal: Student rewards and curriculum-specific regret, learning-progress, replay, or terrain-difficulty rules.
papers.mechanism: Places fourteen curriculum and environment-design methods around a common PPO learner, including easy-start randomization controls. A shared terrain space separates adaptive level selection from simply exposing the learner to easier levels.
papers.evaluation: Runs five simulated quadrupeds with five training seeds per method, evaluating random terrain, unseen structured terrain, hard-level performance, repeatability, and costs.
papers.limitations: Comparisons match student environment steps, not total simulation compute: PAIRED adds an antagonist. One student architecture and robot-specific budgets are used; no physical transfer is tested. No curriculum leads every setting, and easy starts do not explain every held-out-terrain result.

papers.title: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents
papers.code_note: Author README documents memory components and agent callbacks; benchmark environments and verifiers are separate. Not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Historical task requirements, trajectories, submissions, and success/failure feedback support lesson extraction and review.
papers.mechanism: Builds global, approach-level, and implementation-level memories from source attempts. After offline consolidation, the banks are frozen. New tasks receive global and problem-matched guidance; an LLM gate can inject a relevant implementation lesson and check suggestion after tool interactions. Agent weights and tools stay fixed.
papers.evaluation: Uses shared source trajectories and disjoint test problems across PDEAgent-Bench, KernelBenchX, KernelGenBench-MS, and SWE-bench Science, with gate/level ablations and transfer between kernel benchmarks.
papers.limitations: The study uses one solving backbone and agent setup. Gate ablation changes both selection and generated advice. Memory stays frozen during testing, so results do not demonstrate continual online memory improvement. Kernel acceleration counts all test tasks that are both correct and at least 1.01 times faster, and transfer remains within related kernel tasks.

papers.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository README inspected; controlled experiments and coding-agent integrations were not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task rewards support controlled policy training; sampled actions and stronger-teacher probes estimate deployment mismatch.
papers.mechanism: Decomposes regularized return into an interface-specific optimum and policy mismatch under a finite semantic-control model. It tests how presentation or execution changes can alter frozen-model behavior and how further training changes harness rankings.
papers.evaluation: Uses exact-control MiniWoB++ experiments with six harnesses, adaptation and sampling controls, plus five coding harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite.
papers.limitations: The theory assumes a specified KL-regularized control problem. Coding-agent ceilings are stronger-teacher proxies sampled on three tasks, not solved optima. Mismatch estimation requires substantial query budgets; observed ranking agreement does not establish universal prediction or autonomous harness optimization.

papers.title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model
papers.code_note: Paper-linked project and repository README inspected; no model/data download, installation, or execution.
papers.learning_signal: Earlier executed programs paired with terminal logs, exception classes, and validation scores train a separate surrogate.
papers.mechanism: Fine-tunes a world model to predict execution feedback from code and task context. Its predictions guide candidate search, while confidence gates real runs and final submissions remain execution-verified. The trained predictor is reused rather than continually updated during search.
papers.evaluation: Tests prediction on held-out programs and five search policies over seventeen MLE-bench Lite tasks, with three search seeds per task and separate confidence-gating controls.
papers.limitations: Main tasks were seen during surrogate training on roughly 500,000 executions. Base AIDE lacks that corpus knowledge; a corpus-aware agent baseline is untested. Three unseen-task prediction tests do not establish general cross-task search transfer, and prediction errors can misdirect optimization.

papers.title: Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository and README inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Automatically scored paired replays, historical task checks, and model judgments of rule defects or applicability.
papers.mechanism: Repairs role-owned behavioral memories and separately learns conditions for using or avoiding them. A task is scored before its experience updates memory; model weights, roles, and communication structure stay fixed.
papers.evaluation: Tests three multi-agent hosts on four QA, code-generation, and planning benchmarks with one backbone and fixed-order task streams. Baseline figures are inherited from the ConMem study.
papers.limitations: Replay requires repeatable, automatically scored tasks and adds execution cost. Memories are tested individually, missing interactions among rules. Avoidance conditions only accumulate, so mistaken scope judgments can persist; changing teams and task distributions remain untested.

papers.title: CoHARL: Co-Evolving Agent Policies and Executable Harnesses with Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not established in this review; no installation, training, or research execution was performed.
papers.learning_signal: Task rewards and execution traces train a shared policy and guide a separate, stronger harness-code proposer.
papers.mechanism: Collects reinforcement-learning rollouts across a scheduled harness population while periodically proposing executable revisions. Accepted versions enter at update boundaries; a historical accuracy-cost archive informs later proposals.
papers.evaluation: Reports temporally held-out SWE-rebench, transfer to SWE-bench Verified, separately trained Terminal-Bench agents, and controls for search, training, and population use.
papers.limitations: Training framework, evaluator, and action-format family remain fixed. Evidence uses one policy-model setting and single training runs, without confidence intervals or complete total-compute comparisons. Validation reuse and stale archive scores can bias selection; terminal results are not zero-shot SWE transfer.

papers.title: Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
papers.code_note: Author-linked repository inspected; its README says code will be released soon. No runnable release was verified or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Automatically scored task rollouts, gains of inner skill optimizations, and isolated model-review feedback.
papers.mechanism: Encodes skill optimization in an editable meta-skill. An agent uses that procedure to revise task skills and the meta-skill itself, then reuses the refined optimizer across tasks through native skill discovery.
papers.evaluation: Tests 83 SkillsBench tasks and three KernelBench problems, comparing refined versus seed meta-skills, additional model/harness settings, and candidate-budget scaling.
papers.limitations: Scores and budget caps remain external, and reliable automatic verifiers are required. Following the evolving procedure depends on model adherence and review rather than enforced execution. Overall gains vary by domain; finite meta-skill refinement does not establish indefinite accelerating improvement. Task-level training/validation is described, but disjoint meta-training/meta-test tasks are not established by the inspected protocol.

papers.title: The Right Fact, the Wrong Decision: SciValidityBench for Scientific Agent Memory
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository and benchmark README inspected; release tests and model experiments were not run.
papers.learning_signal: Programmatic validity oracles and paired state-changing or corruption-repair controls; no trained update loop is evaluated.
papers.mechanism: Generates scientific histories in which a remembered fact may be invalid to use. A supplied compiler exposes decision-governing relations, separating raw records, retrieval, generic graphs, and compiled-state views.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates 64 task specifications across five validity modules, six domains, and four model families, with counterfactual, repair, and serialization controls.
papers.limitations: Histories and clinical scenarios are synthetic, and compilation rules are supplied. Effects vary by reader and module; richer state sometimes hurts. Curator interpretation: this evaluates state use, not autonomous discovery of validity rules or continual learning in deployed scientists.

papers.title: How Do Coding-Agent Harnesses Self-Evolve? An Empirical Study of Retrospective Adaptation
papers.code_note: The paper links a Zenodo artifact, but its archive page was inaccessible in this review; no code or session artifact was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Completed coding-session traces generate proposals; researchers select changes and define later behavioral checks.
papers.mechanism: Studies individually retained harness adaptations proposed by a retrospective skill, including context instructions and known-failure files. Fresh sessions with and without each change test whether the targeted action recurs on later same-repository issues.
papers.evaluation: Analyzes 125 proposals from thirty SWE-bench Verified sessions, implements twenty-four proposals, and evaluates twelve adaptations in thirteen transfer events, with five sessions per harness.
papers.limitations: Human selection and evaluation remain central. Repeated-work reduction is a behavioral proxy, not proof of better task success or lower latency. Targeted task selection, partly unblinded labeling, one agent, and small samples limit generalization; some changes add unrelated work.

papers.title: When Retrieval Is Not Enough: Obsolete Facts in Agent Memory
papers.venue: Author reports PALM workshop at NeurIPS 2026; primary venue record not verified.
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository and saved-result inventory inspected; experiments and analysis scripts were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: No retained learning update; controlled evidence substitutions and benchmark answers diagnose use of revised facts.
papers.mechanism: Separates retrieving the newest statement from selecting it correctly. Varies BM25 evidence budgets, then replaces an unrelated statement with an obsolete competitor while keeping the latest statement, reader, prompt, and four-statement count fixed.
papers.evaluation: Studies single-hop FactConsolidation at 6K and 32K history lengths. A paired 74-question intervention finds stale-answer failures in two Qwen models despite the correction remaining visible.
papers.limitations: Prompt development reused the intervention cohort. Synthetic stale facts often agree with pretrained world knowledge, so chronology alone is not isolated. Gold-assisted support audits are diagnostic; substring scoring has documented errors. Shared histories, short update chains, and one model family limit generalization.

papers.title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently verified in this review; no research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Human-demonstration guides and generated browser trajectories admitted through privileged environment-state checks.
papers.mechanism: Builds skill-level web tasks and generates verified practice trajectories. A LoRA-trained executor performs short interactions delegated by an untrained planner, so reusable capability is stored in weights rather than an evolving external skill library.
papers.evaluation: Tests ten open-weight agents, held-out MiniWeb websites, and external web benchmarks, comparing skill-only training, planner composition, matched-size task-centric data, and grader validity.
papers.limitations: Skill-only fine-tuning does not improve full-task success and lowers external-benchmark performance; planner composition is essential. Generation uses human guides and privileged site knowledge. Live-web scores use filtered subsets and are not comparable to full benchmark sets; larger-model scaling is untested.

papers.title: Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
papers.code_note: Author-linked repository and README inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction.
papers.learning_signal: Answer sets from executable graph queries, format rewards, and solver-score variance for curriculum difficulty.
papers.mechanism: One shared model alternates between proposing graph-grounded questions and solving them through graph tools. Symbolic task generation and question checks feed alternating proposer and solver reinforcement-learning updates.
papers.evaluation: Reports six benchmarks over Freebase, Wikidata, and an industrial graph, multiple Qwen/Llama backbones, and component and curriculum analyses.
papers.limitations: Training still requires a supplied graph, six query patterns, and pretrained models; language-question verification uses the solver. The current README uses WebQSP/CWQ test questions as validation inputs, so separation from checkpoint selection is not established by this review.

papers.title: CEPO: A General Framework for Improving Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.code_note: The inspected paper plans a code release upon acceptance; no official released implementation was verified.
papers.learning_signal: Training-example feedback and validation scores used by supplied prompt optimizers.
papers.mechanism: Separates a shared coordination prompt from agent-specific execution prompts. Role-aligned instructions guide existing optimizers to tune coordination first, then selected execution prompts, retaining a reusable prompt set around the existing multi-agent system.
papers.evaluation: Applies the framework to four optimizers across eleven document, math, code, and video benchmarks, with guidance-swap, prompt-length, budget, and team-size controls.
papers.limitations: Search algorithms, role guidance, and labeled data remain supplied. Document benchmarks use custom document-level splits and model-judged answers; team-size scaling controls concern one document system. Curator interpretation: this is external prompt optimization, not autonomous redesign of the learning procedure.

papers.title: Agent Memory as Recommendation: Recommender-System Design for Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents
papers.code_note: An official implementation was not independently verified in this review; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Gold evidence-turn annotations from 152 development questions train a separate ranking model.
papers.mechanism: Combines dense/lexical candidates, a learned LightGBM ranker, and token-budget filling to choose stored turns for an answering LLM. Selection avoids generative-model calls; the learned component is the ranker, not the answering model.
papers.evaluation: Tests multi-session LongMemEval-S/M questions and LoCoMo, comparing memory-selection stages, answering accuracy, and serving costs with explicit development/test splits.
papers.limitations: The main LongMemEval stratum excludes unanswerable questions. Near-miss filler can reduce accuracy despite complete evidence; benchmark memory selection is not demonstrated continual learning from deployment. Optional write-time records and answer generation still use LLMs.

papers.title: MultiEvoSkill: Structure-Aware Multi-Agent Skill Evolution for Generalizable Skill Artifacts
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently verified in this review; no research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Multi-model execution traces, reflected issues, and paired parent/candidate scores on fixed selection assignments.
papers.mechanism: Compiles procedural skills into typed graphs, combines debated graph edits, and gates the merged candidate through behavioral, structural, and model-based semantic checks. The retained artifact is frozen for downstream use without model-weight updates.
papers.evaluation: Reports five benchmark comparisons and component ablations. WikiHow, ToolAlpaca, and WebShop use workflow-node F1 adapters; SearchQA uses answer F1 and SpreadsheetBench uses hard instance accuracy.
papers.limitations: Workflow-node scores are not interactive task success. Reused selection data can overfit, semantic review can fail, and configured tolerances permit some regression. The paper’s finite four-epoch search and state-similarity stopping do not prove optimality or monotonic improvement on unseen tasks.

papers.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
papers.code_note: Official runnable implementation was not verified in this review; no research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: comparative analysis of memory construction, retrieval, and downstream use.
papers.mechanism: Compares processed memory with retrieval over raw histories, separating queries helped by memory from queries it loses. Gold-evidence probes, retrieval replay, and writer-reader swaps examine preservation, accessibility, and backbone sensitivity.
papers.evaluation: Tests three long-history memory benchmarks with three backbones, configuration controls, and additional experiential/world-model memory settings; experiential tests freeze training-derived memory.
papers.limitations: Most benchmarks are static, offline, and English; several use subsets. Retrieval scope is normalized by each store rather than equal absolute tokens, and model judges assess answers. Results are configuration- and task-dependent, not proof that memory is generally unnecessary. This differs from the single-conversation MemoryTax paper.

papers.title: EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
papers.code_note: The paper links an anonymous artifact, but its contents were not readable through the available page fetch; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Local interaction traces, task-native episode outcomes, and model-distilled partner profiles and interaction strategies.
papers.mechanism: Pairs each agent with an external MemoryAgent that maintains isolated episodic, semantic, and working state. Turn-level updates inform ongoing actions; episode-end distillation retains reusable interaction knowledge without changing model weights or the memory schema.
papers.evaluation: Compares cooperative coding/reasoning, negotiation, and hidden-role games across five benchmarks, with within/cross-episode ablations and a separate conversational-memory study.
papers.limitations: Several evaluation sets are small; BBH uses one fixed seed. Transferred baseline implementations are adapted to frozen-model conditions, and conversational-memory grading differs from standard LoCoMo. These bounded interactions do not establish safe or indefinite decentralized learning.

papers.title: EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently verified in this review; nothing was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Ground-truth training-task outcomes and model reflection assigning failures to controller, agent, or skill scope.
papers.mechanism: Learns controller routing memory, specialist-agent prompts, and procedural skills through one scoped edit at a time. Programmatic guards constrain edits, while a controller selects memories and synthesizes task-specific execution steps.
papers.evaluation: Uses one fixed-order training pass, then freezes memory for held-out KramaBench, AppWorld, and BBEH-mini evaluations across five backbones, with memory-level and adaptation ablations.
papers.limitations: Accepted edits persist even when the repaired attempt remains unsuccessful. Guards constrain format and scope rather than guaranteeing utility. Test-time comparison arms differ in feedback access and adaptation split, so they do not isolate persistence alone; indefinite online learning is untested.

papers.title: CaliMem: Search-Efficient Data Agent via Calibrated Memory
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently verified in this source review; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Measured downstream training/evaluation scores and residuals against predictions recorded before each curation experiment.
papers.mechanism: Retains evidence and revisable claims throughout a data-curation search. Before evaluating a proposed data policy, the agent predicts its score; observed discrepancies prompt it to narrow or revise claims while the surrounding scaffold remains fixed.
papers.evaluation: Reports biological data-curation tasks and general/code instruction tuning, with memory/prediction ablations and a separate forecasting diagnostic. Searches run for ten or fifteen iterations.
papers.limitations: Each iteration uses one noisy downstream training run and consumes evaluation feedback. Curator interpretation: within-run gains do not establish cross-task learning or uniformly independent final-test selection. Costs grow with downstream training; prediction agreement alone does not verify scientific claims.

papers.title: ReSight: Task-Driven Self-Improving Memory for Embodied Agents
papers.code_note: An official runnable implementation was not verified in this review; no research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Retained sensory evidence, executor failures, and coding-agent exploration/replay without task reference answers.
papers.mechanism: Preserves robot keyframes while a coding agent builds reusable memory-processing programs, query tools, and skills. Explore–Distill–Mount registers these capabilities for a fixed execution model and adds derived memory fields for later queries.
papers.evaluation: Studies GOAT-core retrieval, OC-NaVQA and FindingDory expansion, separate frozen-capability reuse on held-out episodes, and queries over real robot patrol memories.
papers.limitations: The main FindingDory expansion uses exploration episodes; separate excluded episodes test reuse. Exploration has a larger independent compute budget. Real-robot memory-query scores are separate from downstream physical execution, and repeated expansion under changing long-term demand remains untested.

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not established in this review; no installation, training, or research execution was performed.
papers.learning_signal: Self-generated questions, candidate answers and reasoning traces, consistency filters, and token distributions from a privileged EMA teacher.
papers.mechanism: Seeds generation with broad topics, removes unstable or already-solved questions, and self-distills on student rollouts. Student and teacher weights carry across rounds; the teacher is an exponential average rather than an external stronger model.
papers.evaluation: Compares training objectives on shared synthetic data, language reasoning and out-of-domain retention, visual question answering, and hallucination benchmarks, with filtering and teacher-context ablations.
papers.limitations: Data-free refers to curated textual questions and answers: topics are hand-chosen and visual training requires unlabeled images. Consistent mistakes can pass verification. Retention is mixed: the all-domain mixture improves the average but loses 4.9 points on MATH-500; small-model tests do not establish unbounded improvement.

papers.title: FlexA-Mem: Budget-Adaptive Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: New history records and current queries; rendering follows a fixed rule.
papers.mechanism: Keeps an immutable history store and constructs a query-specific context from a timeline plus retrieved detail under a fixed token budget. Its fixed rendering rules provide a useful baseline for learned memory systems.
papers.evaluation: The abstract reports AppWorld task-completion experiments and LongMemEval and LoCoMo QA, including an unused-task evaluation with predictions fixed beforehand.
papers.limitations: The method adapts the presented context rather than learning its own update policy. It is included as an adjacent comparison for separating memory access gains from agent self-learning.

papers.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents
papers.code_note: Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: a decision-theoretic and empirical analysis of memory value.

papers.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning

papers.limitations: Fast memory resets each episode and summary history resets each trial; this is not persistent learning across deployment tasks. ML10/ML45 expose goal coordinates, and nonstationary task streams remain future work. Attention aggregation is quadratic in episode count even though timestep processing is linear.

papers.title: Recursive Self-Improvement on a Budget: Scoring Code Edits Before They Run

Curator interpretation: matching checker evaluations does not establish equal total proposal, token, or wall-clock cost; this does not demonstrate an evolving improver.

papers.title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory

Costs depend on prices and caching; the small study cannot establish that designed memory is generally unnecessary.

papers.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims

papers.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?

The retrieval baseline always injects its nearest memory without a similarity threshold; global edits and conflicting workflows expose different failure modes, not a universal impossibility result.

papers.title: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents

papers.limitations: Experiments reuse a fixed experience pool rather than an online-growing memory. Recall-policy contrasts do not reach p<0.05 at this sample size; several secondary conditions run once. Retrieval baselines use different configurations, and stronger agents can be harmed by memory. All tasks retrieve same-repository experience; similarity to gold patches was not measured.

papers.title: MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Author-linked public repository page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Downstream task-success rewards from complete agent interactions, plus selection-size and output-format penalties.
papers.mechanism: Trains a memory-composition policy to choose the number, identity, and ordering of retrieved experiences. GRPO-based Experience Policy Optimization updates the composer while keeping the executor, retriever, and memory bank fixed.
papers.evaluation: Reports three tau-squared-bench domains with 4B and 8B executors, memory-token costs, ordering ablations, and transfer across domains, executors, and memory sources.
papers.limitations: This is external policy training, not continual growth of the memory bank. Frontier-scale executors and non-procedural memories are untested; sequence rewards confound selection and ordering, and several per-executor performance-gap confidence intervals include zero.

papers.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
papers.code_note: Author repository and README inspected; not installed or executed. Its documented network defaults require separate evaluation-contamination controls.
papers.learning_signal: Contrasts between executions of candidate and reference harnesses, interpreted by model-based editors and reflection.
papers.mechanism: Proposes and probes harness edits on the current task, then composes a successor. Adopted harnesses and evidence-linked lessons enter a persistent library that guides later improvements; each new task starts from the common base harness.
papers.evaluation: Tests WorkBuddy-Bench, JobBench, and Legal Agent Benchmark across two models and two initial harnesses, with recursion budgets, component ablations, and library-transfer analyses.
papers.limitations: Behavioral contrasts do not verify correctness and can share model biases. Stage instructions, decision rules, and model weights remain fixed while the library evolves. Extra probes incur inference cost; benchmark gains do not establish unrestricted or indefinitely improving autonomy.

papers.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Matched execution outcomes, hypothesis uncertainty, experiment cost, and later improvement used to train a memory manager.
papers.mechanism: Selects informative trials over code/skill hypotheses and retains successful revisions in hierarchical memory. A PPO-trained manager learns memory actions while the robot foundation model and memory operator remain frozen during evolution.
papers.evaluation: Reports RoboCasa365 and LIBERO-Pro with disjoint evolution/evaluation seeds, component ablations, and transfer of the simulation-evolved harness to five physical SO-101 tasks.
papers.limitations: “Zero-shot” concerns the harness: the real-robot SmolVLA backbone was first fine-tuned on fifty human demonstrations per task. Thirty trials per condition/task and bounded benchmarks do not establish indefinite retention or improvement of the outer selection procedure.

papers.title: ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience
papers.code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
papers.learning_signal: Completed execution trajectories accepted by an environment verifier, with action-validity feedback.
papers.mechanism: After one scored attempt per task, a frozen copy of the initial model reads accepted experience with hindsight. Its token distributions train persistent LoRA adapters for subsequent tasks; invalid-action turns are removed from the privileged teacher input.
papers.evaluation: The authors report success, interaction cost, ablations, and held-out scene transfer on ALFWorld and WebShop with two model sizes, plus AppWorld experiments.
papers.limitations: The method needs an available verifier and update compute. WebShop adaptation accepts scores of at least 0.9 although reported exact success requires 1.0; outcome acceptance does not identify causally useful actions or prove a shortest solution.

papers.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
papers.code_note: Official repository and README inspected; released harnesses and result files were not independently audited or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Executed draft checks, failure replay and perturbation, training regressions, and validation summaries.
papers.mechanism: Updates an executor harness and the optimizer's own prompts, skills, tools, hooks, and notes. Verification tools test proposed fixes and diagnoses before submission while both models remain frozen.
papers.evaluation: Adds VERSE to four reimplemented harness optimizers, evaluating held-out SWE-rebench and newer multilingual tasks; also studies Terminal-Bench and component ablations.
papers.limitations: Selection rules and core verification tools remain fixed. Matched candidate counts do not imply equal total compute. Reimplemented baselines differ from their original systems; self-evolution benefits vary by host, and noisy outcome changes often fail to reproduce.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Author-linked repository and setup documentation inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: An external judge flags harmful completed trajectories; model components synthesize and organize defensive policies.
papers.mechanism: Stores failure episodes and distills them into a hierarchical policy memory. Relevant policies condition later tasks while the acting model stays frozen.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate eight benchmarks spanning jailbreaks, prompt injection, and coding, plus adaptive attackers and a frozen-memory control. Each benchmark starts with empty memory; updates occur only after completed episodes.
papers.limitations: The reported protocol does not establish cross-benchmark retention. Retrieval and enforcement failures remain, and learning depends on the external judge. DTap additionally uses a pre-tool guard, which must be retained when interpreting comparisons.

papers.title: Learn Now, Use Next, Trust Later: Prequential Test-Time Learning for LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
papers.learning_signal: Observed action transitions and prospective checks of predicted effects in later, non-source episodes.
papers.mechanism: Extracts testable policy hypotheses that can guide the next decision, while keeping persistent reuse behind an evidence gate. Candidate predictions are frozen before later observations; counterevidence can withdraw promoted guidance. Model weights remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: The paper compares two actor configurations and learning baselines across five rounds on WebArena-Lite and ALFWorld, including first-attempt analysis, safeguards ablations, and costs.
papers.limitations: Evaluation repeats tasks and excludes ten WebArena-Lite cases. Promotion relies on environment-specific evidence adapters; predictive validation does not by itself establish causal policy utility. Longer changing streams remain future work.

papers.title: SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Binary verifier outcomes for the incumbent and candidate skill on the same validation items.
papers.mechanism: Retains skill edits only when paired wins outweigh penalized regressions, an exact binomial test rejects the null, and a regression cap is satisfied. The acting model and edit proposer remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: Compares the gate with the same SkillOpt proposer across five benchmarks and four backbones, including component ablations and reported matched proposal/token budgets.
papers.limitations: Error control is per fixed comparison; reuse of validation data does not provide a trajectory-level guarantee. Thresholds still require held-out tuning, and tests assume binary outcomes. Multimodal and multi-agent transfer remain untested.

papers.title: Which Self-Improvements Should We Trust? Reliable Self-Improvement When Agents Reuse Their Benchmarks
papers.code_note: Official runnable implementation was not verified in this review; no research code was executed.

Audit certificates stay hidden from the proposer; the paper derives simultaneous guarantees under an independent evaluation sample and decision-only feedback.
papers.evaluation: Tests LLM-proposed classification-pipeline revisions on Covertype for 200 rounds and 30 seeds per evaluation-set size; a separate holdout estimates accepted improvements.
papers.limitations: Guarantees require bounded scores, an independent identically distributed evaluation sample, and strict feedback isolation. Experiments concern classification, and baselines are adapted styles rather than original agent systems. Finite holdout estimates are not known population truth; coding-agent and safety-metric transfer remain untested.

Transfer differs by backbone: a non-game data control performs better on Mistral. These tests do not establish indefinite self-improvement.

papers.title: Self-Play Search Distillation for Large Language Model Reasoning

papers.evaluation: Tests four source games, fifteen disjoint held-out games, six mathematics suites, rule variants, and training-duration comparisons across Qwen and Llama configurations.
papers.limitations: Supervision depends on engineered games and external search experts. Mathematical results mix pass@1 and AVG@32 protocols, transfer varies by backbone, and longer supervised training can lose earlier gains. Curator interpretation: replay validity is not proof of globally optimal decisions.

papers.title: What Stops Recursive Self-Improvement in Robotics? Lessons from 123 Rounds of Agentic Skill Discovery

papers.evaluation: Reports one 123-round RoboCasa experiment over three kitchen tasks with an additional held-out task. Some local skills improve, but the target fridge task never succeeds; the record analyzes early-step bottlenecks and evaluator failures.
papers.limitations: One simulator, layout, and unreplicated run provide no matched-budget causal estimate. Human repairs and model/provider changes share the timeline. Suggested design remedies are hypotheses, and simulated skill discovery is not evidence of autonomous real-robot learning or improvement of the outer evaluation procedure.

papers.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents

papers.mechanism: Searches research-agent harness rewrites, retaining the best incumbent for further edits. The editable agent controls search and context management; the outer selection rule remains fixed.
papers.evaluation: Reports seven accepted rewrites in the main eight-day run, transfer to ALE-Bench, MLE-Bench, FML-Bench and WeatherBench 2, and a separate comparison using an evolved agent as the outer optimizer.
papers.limitations: The outer-optimizer comparison is inconclusive with three seeds per arm. Noisy grades can accept false improvements. Harness gains do not establish accelerating self-improvement or independent reproduction.

papers.title: SelfOp: An Optimization Algorithm for Self-Improving Security Agents
papers.code_note: Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Execution outcomes, vulnerability metadata, and cross-instance agreement among textual critiques.
papers.mechanism: Traces errors backward through outcomes, trajectories, and context, then clusters critiques to revise persistent skill instructions and reference documents. Model weights and the execution harness remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: Studies CyberGym vulnerability reproduction, component ablations, checkpoint selection, and cross-model transfer; the held-out test subset contains 80 tasks.
papers.limitations: Evaluation covers a cost-limited benchmark subset. Baselines are adapted to shared supervision. Stopping avoids validation during the final optimization run, but its noise floor and window were empirically calibrated using earlier runs with validation scoring. Other security tasks remain future work.

papers.title: Reflections on Trusting Trust, Revisited: Contaminating Self-Modifying AI Coding Agents with Poisoned Benchmarks
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Benchmark feedback during the self-modification process.
papers.mechanism: Studies whether poisoned optimization benchmarks can induce persistent changes that cause self-modifying coding agents to emit vulnerable code on later clean tasks.
papers.evaluation: Presents proof-of-concept studies on a modified Darwin Gödel Machine, SICA, and Hyperagents, including continued evolution after poison removal.
papers.limitations: These are constructed attacks under specified agent and benchmark conditions, not an estimate of attack prevalence. Clean subsequent tasks do not reliably remove contaminated components in the studied cases.

papers.title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Contrasts between successful and failed trajectories, followed by validation gates.

papers.limitations: The reported benchmark separation depends on the documented curation and similarity-screening procedure. Infrastructure is outside the editable scope, and downstream evaluation allows function selection but no further function modification.

papers.title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Author-linked public repository page inspected; no installation, execution, or dataset download.
papers.learning_signal: Accumulated interaction trajectories and language-model judgments of shared workflows and reusable skills.
papers.mechanism: Clusters trajectories by procedural workflow, updates and splits clusters as experience grows, and distills transferable skills. Inference retrieves both environment-aligned examples and abstract skills without retraining the acting model.
papers.evaluation: Uses ten environments across embodied action, tools, search, data analysis, and browsing, with 12,489 training and 1,230 test instances; measures performance, backward transfer, ablations, and two held-out transfer settings.
papers.limitations: Experience construction includes model-generated and human-reviewed trajectories, rather than only autonomous deployment experience. Task order affects outcomes, and some domain/backbone combinations retain negative backward transfer. Million-experience deployment efficiency is not established.

papers.title: Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

papers.evaluation: Reviews evidence for admission, retrieval, activation, containment, and repair; identifies comparatively weak evidence for repairing descendants and evaluating resumed learning.
papers.limitations: The framework proposes how to organize longitudinal safety assessment; it does not certify that a learning system remains safe.

papers.title: Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses
papers.code_note: Official repository and paper-specific reproducibility guide inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Execution failures, tool-state traces, and separate repair/gate scores before final held-out evaluation.
papers.mechanism: Clusters failures and routes repairs to prompts, tool-boundary middleware, or both. Evolution retains candidates on a Pareto frontier while the underlying model stays fixed.
papers.evaluation: Compares harness optimizers on BFCL multi-round and tau2 Retail/Telecom, measuring held-out lift, repeatability, costs, and an empirical lower-tail selection metric.
papers.limitations: Telecom PRISM arms use a different scoring orchestration path from comparison arms. Lower-tail estimates are not guarantees; budgets count inner rollouts, and the study does not evaluate repeated deployment cycles or unrestricted harness rewrites.

papers.title: MASkills: Continual Skills Optimization for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.code_note: Author-linked public repository and README inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Team task outcomes, LLM judgments of individual skill contributions, and validation performance.
papers.mechanism: Uses a separate critic and optimizer to refine, induce, merge, or prune persistent skill artifacts for cooperating agents. Aggregated textual feedback is smoothed across cycles; a validation gate rolls back edits that fail its acceptance threshold.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates HotpotQA, LoCoMo, and GAIA, with transferred skill libraries, actor/topology variations, and operator ablations.
papers.limitations: Its gradient and momentum terminology describes language-space analogies, not differentiable model training. Skill attribution depends on critic judgments and researchers supply validation tasks. Benchmark transfer does not establish indefinite retention under changing deployments.

papers.title: Control-Data Flow Separation: Stable Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.code_note: Author reference implementation and README inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task outcomes and per-example feedback on multi-agent interaction traces.
papers.mechanism: Keeps routing, formatting, and termination schemas outside the optimizer’s editable prompt surface. Typed validation rejects malformed control before routing while textual feedback improves task-facing prompts.
papers.evaluation: Tests BIG-Bench Hard subsets, collaborative paper-review generation, and synthetic insurance-rating workflows, with schema/retry ablations and smaller cross-model comparisons.
papers.limitations: Eventual protocol validity can include retries and does not imply correct decisions. Roles and schemas remain fixed; review quality uses an LLM judge, and additional model-family comparisons use one seed. Insurance experiments do not establish operational suitability.

papers.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Old and new task demonstrations, observation-representation overlap, and disagreement between predicted and labeled actions.
papers.mechanism: Selects old experiences near new-task observations that require conflicting actions, then enriches the replay buffer with these anchors during sequential policy training. Retention changes through both replay selection and policy updates.
papers.evaluation: The authors test removal and enrichment of anchors on four LIBERO suites, diffusion and VLA policies, and two real-robot sequences involving jars and sweater folding, with buffer-selection ablations.
papers.limitations: Extraction requires policy latents and past training data, and recomputing their representations has a cost. Sequences contain only three to ten tasks; retention on these settings does not establish indefinite continual deployment.

papers.title: CIDER: Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Current-task rewards, human demonstrations and corrective interventions, plus a frozen prior actor’s action distributions on archived states.

papers.evaluation: Reports sequential acquisition and retention across six real-robot household and industrial manipulation tasks, with evaluation after each stage and gradient-routing, initialization, and sampling ablations.
papers.limitations: This is human-assisted, reward-driven acquisition on short-horizon tasks. Longer tasks with sparse rewards or delayed failures may need additional supervision; the six-task result does not establish unbounded skill accumulation.

papers.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.

papers.title: HyperSkill: Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Hypergraph-Structured Skill Memory

papers.title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses

papers.title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement

papers.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

papers.title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks

papers.title: AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?

papers.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
