papers.title: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Paired candidate/incumbent correctness on development instances.
papers.mechanism: Places a sequential statistical gate between proposed prompt edits and retention. A betting-based evidence process accepts an edit only after its paired outcomes cross a threshold; otherwise the incumbent remains.
papers.evaluation: Author experiments use Qwen2.5 prompt evolution on GSM8K, SVAMP, and ARC-Challenge, with planted-gain and stochastic regimes and a separate audit pool. Statistical gates reduce noisy commitments relative to greedy selection.
papers.limitations: The guarantee is per candidate under a conditional paired-null assumption, not a guarantee for the whole adaptive search. Experiments cover one model family and prompt edits; the finite audit and development-set coverage limit interpretation. Small genuine gains may be rejected.

papers.title: Membrane: A Self-Evolving Contrastive Safety Memory for LLM Agent Defense
papers.code_note: Author repository README inspected; research code and attack data were not executed or downloaded.
papers.learning_signal: Paired harmful/benign examples, guard decisions, and feedback about jailbreaks or false refusals.
papers.mechanism: An external guard retrieves cells pairing unsafe conditions with benign exceptions. A planner and writer revise the cell store under structural validation, while model weights remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: Reports HarmBench and AgentHarm tests with development-set memory frozen for primary comparisons, plus separate evolving-memory streams, transfer, poisoning, and component studies.
papers.limitations: AgentHarm headline metrics measure refusal/admission, not completed harmful tool actions. Online streams receive preconstructed benign counterparts. Text-only English tests and limited attacker capabilities do not establish robustness against an adversary controlling both guard prompts and memory.

papers.title: On the Generalization Gap in Self-Evolving Language Model Reasoning
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently verified in this review; no research implementation was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Preference labels and revision feedback generated by the same base model from supplied unlabeled prompts; oracle labels form comparison arms.
papers.mechanism: Compares single-round verification, feedback-guided revision, repeated preference training, and curricula inside a controlled generator-verifier loop. Retained changes are trained policy weights rather than an evolving agent harness.
papers.evaluation: Studies easy-to-hard Knights and Knaves reasoning and OpenThoughts-based training with mathematical/generalization tests. Gains often plateau below oracle supervision; a larger-model revision condition nearly closes the gap.
papers.limitations: The restricted offline setup is not an impossibility result for all self-improvement. Open-ended tests cannot isolate verifier error from prompt-distribution shifts, and online-RL comparison rows use different starting models and supervision. Improved pass@1 with nearly unchanged pass@32 limits claims about expanded solution coverage.

papers.title: PEAM: Parametric Embodied Agent Memory through Contrastive Internalization of Experience in Minecraft
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not established in this source review; nothing was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Verified successful trajectories, matched failure-correction pairs, and failure statistics used by fixed consolidation gates.
papers.mechanism: A deliberative model collects experience for category-specific LoRA adapters. Behavioral cloning and trajectory-preference training internalize selected skills; the fast adapter path falls back to deliberation when verification fails.
papers.evaluation: Inspected preprint v2 tests eleven Minecraft tasks over three seeds, sequential craft/gather/combat consolidation, cost, and trigger ablations. Official publication metadata confirms the renamed Findings paper; its PDF was not inspected.
papers.limitations: The forgetting test concerns three isolated categories, not general within-category retention. Consolidation rules remain fixed, adapter storage grows with categories, and trigger robustness uses re-sliced trajectories. No real-robot transfer is evaluated.

papers.title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Accumulated skill-use experience and feedback from evaluating created skills.
papers.mechanism: Manages a skill lifecycle spanning creation, storage, retrieval, evaluation, and refinement. Per-skill experience persists across tasks so later attempts can reuse and adapt earlier work.
papers.evaluation: The revised abstract reports SkillsBench and SkillLearnBench comparisons and transfer of generated skills to another agent.
papers.limitations: The comparison with human-authored skills is explicitly reported on a successfully covered subset. Interpretation: that subset result should not be presented as an overall advantage across all tasks.

papers.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
papers.code_note: Paper-linked project and official repository inspected; newer SkillOpt-Sleep features are separate from the reviewed paper experiments. Not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Scored task rollouts, optimizer-model critiques, and separate selection-set scores gate retained text edits.
papers.mechanism: An external optimizer revises one skill document through bounded edits, rejected-edit memory, and slow epoch-level updates. The target model and execution harness stay fixed; a selected text artifact is reused on later tasks.
papers.evaluation: Reports six benchmarks, seven target models, and direct-chat/Codex/Claude Code settings, plus component, budget, and nearby model/harness/task-transfer comparisons.
papers.limitations: Requires reliable scoring and selection data plus substantial optimization calls. Zero extra deployment model calls does not mean zero training cost. A single skill can be insufficient for heterogeneous domains, and near-domain transfer is not unrestricted continual improvement.

papers.title: optimize_anything: A Universal API for Optimizing any Text Parameter
papers.venue: ACM CAIS 2026 reported in paper and author artifact; publisher record inaccessible
papers.code_note: Paper-linked GEPA framework and separate author artifact repository inspected; neither executed or reproduced.
papers.learning_signal: Supplied evaluator scores and domain-specific diagnostics such as execution traces, errors, and per-example results.
papers.mechanism: Exposes single-task search, shared multi-task search, and reusable-artifact optimization through one interface. Its default GEPA backend retains a Pareto frontier and uses reflective proposals to revise textual artifacts around fixed models.
papers.evaluation: Reports coding-agent skills, agent architecture, prompt learning, cloud scheduling, kernel generation, and mathematical optimization, with feedback, transfer, and proposer ablations.
papers.limitations: Evaluators and diagnostic feedback require domain expertise. Multi-task search can hurt unrelated problems, as in circle packing; proposal quality and evaluation cost vary. Curator interpretation: a general optimization interface does not establish autonomous improvement of its search algorithm.

papers.title: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Evaluates whether memory systems recover environment-specific facts, state changes, workflows, pitfalls, and premise conditions from past web-agent trajectories.
papers.evaluation: Compares retrieval and coding-agent evidence gathering on questions derived from specialized environments, including accuracy and latency tradeoffs.
papers.limitations: This is a context-gathering and question-answering benchmark. Better answers do not alone demonstrate successful live task execution or sustained autonomous skill acquisition; the paper is marked work in progress.

papers.title: Ask Only When Needed: Proactive Retrieval from Memory and Skills for Experience-Driven Lifelong Agents
papers.code_note: An official implementation was not independently verified in this review; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Environment rewards, paired retrieval/no-retrieval continuations, and interaction-length penalties.
papers.mechanism: Interleaves GRPO policy updates with typed factual, episodic, and skill-memory extraction. Replaying a shared interaction prefix creates a no-retrieval branch whose outcome helps train the timing and content of later retrieval actions.
papers.evaluation: Reports SciWorld, AlfWorld, and StuLife experiments, memory/policy ablations, retrieval costs, and two Qwen2.5 model sizes. StuLife uses online evolution without a supplied training split.
papers.limitations: Requires reward-bearing environments and prefix replay; the training pipeline includes supervised cold-start trajectories and a separate extraction model. The paired reward is a shaped empirical signal, not an unbiased causal-effect estimator. Long-term open-world retention is not established.

papers.title: SkillFlow:Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Trajectories, task outcomes, and evaluation rubrics.
papers.mechanism: Starts agents without skills and carries a library of trajectory- and rubric-derived skill patches through sequential tasks within task families.
papers.evaluation: Measures task success, skill discovery, revision, and reuse across a structured set of task families, with benefits differing substantially across models.
papers.limitations: Skill invocation is not evidence of useful learning: the paper reports high use with small gains or regression. Family-specific evaluation does not establish broad transfer.

papers.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills
papers.code_note: Author repository, paper backlink, layout, and setup documentation inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Verified task outcomes, skill interface/replay checks, and observed downstream utility.
papers.mechanism: Compiles successful workflows into persistent executable skills. Later tasks either replay compatible skills or use them as context for new workflows; lifecycle rules restrict or suppress harmful reuse without updating model weights.
papers.evaluation: Reports ALFWorld, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, and MATH-500 comparisons, a backbone sweep, and admission/curation ablations. Main streams accumulate skills online; separate fixed-bank MBPP analyses test reuse mechanisms.
papers.limitations: Correctness feedback or tests are available in the studied domains; signal-free tasks remain outside scope. Full-split MBPP router comparisons are not statistically separated. Long-running bank maintenance and adversarial feedback remain open.

papers.title: On Safety Risks in Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this review; no implementation was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Benign execution experience and, in mixed-stream experiments, execution or refusal experiences retained by the evaluated frameworks.
papers.mechanism: Studies safety changes when offline Agent Workflow Memory or online ReasoningBank supplies accumulated experience to frozen models. Varying experience size and a length-matched prompt control probe the contribution of retrieved content.
papers.evaluation: Tests web and simulated household settings using BrowserART, Agent-SafetyBench, and SafeAgentBench, with several model backbones and mixed benign/harmful experience streams.
papers.limitations: Results cover two frameworks and finite runs up to 800 steps, using automated safety grading. Refusal experience reduces unsafe behavior but can increase over-refusal. Curator interpretation: attribution and prompt controls support a bounded explanation, not universal causality or inevitable failure of every learning agent.

papers.title: Combee: Scaling Prompt Learning for Self-Improving Language Model Agents
papers.code_note: Author blog describes ACE/GEPA integrations; a pinned runnable paper implementation was not independently verified or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Textual reflections from task executions, downstream scores, and measured iteration latency.
papers.mechanism: Adds a scaling layer to existing generate-reflect-update methods: hierarchical parallel aggregation, duplicated/shuffled reflections, and latency-based batch selection produce reusable context updates without weight training.
papers.evaluation: Tests ACE and GEPA on AppWorld, Terminal-Bench, Formula, and FiNER, including held-out tasks, aggregation controls, cost measurements, and selected repeated-run analyses.
papers.limitations: The largest speedup does not preserve identical accuracy: Terminal-Bench Combee scores below sequential ACE. Rare or conflicting reflections can still be lost. The batch controller uses single-trial profiling and a fixed threshold; asynchronous execution and broader framework transfer remain untested.

papers.title: APEX-EM: Non-Parametric Online Learning for Autonomous Agents via Structured Procedural-Episodic Experience Replay
papers.code_note: The inspected v3 promises an artifact release; no official repository was verified and no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task verification and teacher-model scores/feedback on completed successful and failed executions.
papers.mechanism: Stores procedural-episodic traces in a typed graph and retrieves them by semantic, structural, and graph signals. A plan/retrieve/generate/iterate/ingest loop separates within-task repair from retaining experience without weight updates.
papers.evaluation: Version 3 evaluates code, structured queries, HLE, Lifelong Agent Bench, and ALFWorld. It distinguishes recurring training tasks from held-out transfer using frozen memory and adds same-backbone comparisons.
papers.limitations: Cumulative success means solved at least once across repeated epochs, not first-attempt generalization. Teacher/verifier feedback and domain adapters remain inputs; cross-backbone reference rows are not controlled comparisons. Monotonic storage growth alone does not establish freedom from forgetting.

papers.title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
papers.code_note: Official repository inspected; it provides two reference experiments and links a separate TerminalBench artifact. Not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task scores and filesystem-accessible source code and execution traces from prior candidates.
papers.mechanism: An external coding-agent proposer inspects earlier harness implementations and failures, then revises context, memory, retrieval, or tool-loop code. A population and Pareto frontier retain reusable harnesses around frozen models.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates online text classification, retrieval-augmented mathematical reasoning, and TerminalBench-2; classification and math include transfer to new datasets or models.
papers.limitations: TerminalBench-2 uses the same 89 tasks for search and final scoring, unlike the held-out transfer experiments. Results depend on one strong proposer, and current cleaned-up source is not an independently verified reproduction.

papers.title: From Static Templates to Dynamic Runtime Graphs: A Survey of Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Official implementation availability was not established in this review; no code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: literature synthesis and evaluation framework.
papers.mechanism: Organizes workflow optimization by when structure is determined, which components change, and which feedback governs changes. Separates reusable templates, per-run graphs, and execution traces.
papers.evaluation: Proposes reporting that combines downstream task performance with structural properties, cost, robustness, and variation across inputs.
papers.limitations: A taxonomy and reporting proposal do not independently validate surveyed methods. Runtime graph changes can be specific to one task and should not automatically be interpreted as persistent learning.

papers.title: Hyperagents
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Task evaluation and archived improvement histories, including transfer tests for the meta-agent.
papers.mechanism: Combines the task solver and the agent that modifies it in one editable program. DGM-Hyperagents can therefore revise their own improvement procedure as well as task-solving code.
papers.evaluation: Studies coding, paper-review prediction, robotics reward design, and math-solution grading. The reviewed v2 separately transfers the task agent and meta agent; meta-only transfer recovers nearly all combined-transfer benefit in its 50-iteration math-grading test.
papers.limitations: The transfer test holds the meta agent fixed while it generates task-agent variants. Initial math graders fail output formatting, affecting the starting score. Main experiments retain fixed task distributions and outer selection/evaluation; bounded transfer does not establish unbounded or self-accelerating improvement.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently verified in this source review; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Supervised assistant-token targets from environment trajectories, augmented with retrieved experience during LoRA training.
papers.mechanism: Trains the policy to use full retrieved trajectories instead of adding memory only at inference. The main retrieval bank stays read-only; separate experiments reuse a first attempt as context for a second without parameter updates.
papers.evaluation: Compares inference-only retrieval and retrieval-aware fine-tuning on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld, including easy-to-hard task-group transfer, retrieval ablations, and imperfect or self-generated experience.
papers.limitations: Main hard-task evaluations retrieve matched hard-task expert traces despite easy-only policy training. Self-experience covers one retry and hurts ScienceWorld despite helping ALFWorld. Cross-paper headline comparisons are qualitative; long-term heterogeneous memory accumulation is not evaluated.

papers.title: AutoSkill: Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning via Skill Self-Evolution
papers.code_note: Official repository linked by the paper and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Dialogue histories, recurring user preferences, corrections, and model judgments about extraction and merging.
papers.mechanism: Extracts explicit instruction skills from interactions, retrieves them for later requests, and merges related updates into versioned skill artifacts. A persistent skill bank changes while the underlying language model stays fixed.
papers.evaluation: The inspected v2 reports SkillBank statistics from four language/model subsets of WildChat and qualitative examples of extracted and repeatedly revised skills.
papers.limitations: Artifact counts and case studies demonstrate construction and maintenance, not a controlled estimate of improved downstream task success or long-term retention. This AutoSkill is distinct from MUSE-Autoskill and similarly named video-QA work.

papers.title: EvoX: Meta-Evolution for Automated Discovery
papers.code_note: Official SkyDiscover repository linked by the paper and inspected; it also contains other algorithms. Not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task-evaluator scores, execution artifacts, and changes in population performance over search windows.
papers.mechanism: Co-evolves candidate programs and the search strategy that selects parents, variation operators, and examples. Stagnation triggers strategy revisions informed by earlier strategies and current population state.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates 196 mathematical, systems, and algorithmic optimization tasks, with three runs and generally 100 iterations for open-framework comparisons.
papers.limitations: Search adapts within each optimization problem; cross-task lifelong retention is not established. AlphaEvolve comparisons use published scores with an undisclosed iteration budget. Evaluators and outer monitoring rules remain supplied.

papers.title: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
papers.code_note: Paper-linked preview repository README inspected; no environment or memory service was installed or run.
papers.learning_signal: Earlier task actions and observations supply experience needed for later dependent subtasks.
papers.mechanism: Constructs multi-session tasks in which earlier choices and discoveries constrain later execution. Persistent memory connects sessions; comparisons separate long-context history, external memory systems, and retrieval-based stores.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates bundled shopping, group travel, progressive search, and sequential mathematical/physical reasoning using completion, progress, dependency-depth, and latency measures.
papers.limitations: These constructed task chains do not establish indefinite lifelong learning. Benefits vary by backend and domain; low task success can reflect reasoning or planning failures as well as memory. Section 4.3 describes gains in web search and formal reasoning, but Table 3 shows backend- and metric-dependent effects.

papers.title: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2026 acceptance reported by authors; venue record not inspected
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task rewards, teacher-generated skill distillation, and validation failures.
papers.mechanism: Distills successful and failed trajectories into a hierarchical skill library, retrieves those skills during policy training, and adds lessons from validation failures. The library and model policy change together during reinforcement learning.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate ALFWorld, WebShop, and seven search-augmented QA datasets, including component and teacher-model analyses.
papers.limitations: The method uses a teacher and reward-bearing environments, so it is not training-free or supervision-free. Interpretation: its recursive skill refresh is not evidence that the system can redesign its own learning algorithm.

papers.title: Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Shared experience across a group of agent variants and coding-task evaluations.
papers.mechanism: Treats a group of agents as the unit of evolution, allowing discoveries from different branches to influence later designs. It aims to reuse exploratory diversity that would otherwise remain isolated in individual lineages.
papers.evaluation: Evaluations use SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot, with model-transfer and framework-bug recovery analyses.
papers.limitations: The evidence concerns coding agents under the study budgets. Curator interpretation: experience sharing during search is distinct from a deployed multi-agent team continually learning in an open environment.

papers.title: TAME: A Trustworthy Test-Time Evolution of Agent Memory with Systematic Benchmarking
papers.code_note: Author repository README links the paper and describes a small smoke-test sample; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Accurate binary task-outcome feedback, evaluator judgments of memory contribution, and model-generated trust annotations.
papers.mechanism: An executor retrieves useful experiences with risk guidance from a shared memory bank. An evaluator revises reuse priorities after outcomes, while new experiences enter with trust annotations; model weights remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: Trust-Memevo evolves initially empty memory on benign science, math, tool-use, and coding streams using two backbones, then freezes memory for separate trustworthiness tests.
papers.limitations: The inspected v2 uses a shared bank, differing from the initial dual-memory description. Aggregate trust scores need not reflect every safety dimension. Evaluation is text-only, and accurate outcome feedback is supplied; this does not certify safe open-ended adaptation.

papers.title: Reasoning Cache: Continual Improvement Over Long Horizons via Short-Horizon RL
papers.code_note: Author repository README inspected; inference/training code and checkpoints were not installed, downloaded, or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Correctness rewards on supplied mathematical prompt-answer pairs, with generated reasoning summaries reused during training.
papers.mechanism: Alternates bounded reasoning attempts with summary updates for the same problem. GRPO trains summary-conditioned generation, and a replay buffer supplies later-turn summaries; inference expands the reasoning budget without updating weights.
papers.evaluation: Tests mathematical benchmarks and FrontierScience, budget extrapolation, summary/replay ablations, and integration with other inference scaffolds. The main trained model uses a two-stage mathematics curriculum.
papers.limitations: Continual improvement here is longer within-problem inference, not persistent deployment learning. Myopic rewards can miss exploration useful only later, and summarization quality depends on the backbone. Version 2 changes IMO-AnswerBench grading after the earlier parser rejected valid answers.

papers.title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2026 acceptance reported by authors; official title listing found but article record not inspected
papers.code_note: Author-linked repository README inspected; current source was not executed or audited as a pinned paper reproduction.
papers.learning_signal: Downstream F1 or task success trains a separate skill-selection controller; hard training cases guide LLM-authored skill revisions.
papers.mechanism: A PPO-trained controller selects memory-operation skills for a fixed executor. A fixed designer periodically refines the skill bank, with rollback based on stabilized training rewards. The skills describe how to remember, rather than the memories themselves.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates conversational memory and ALFWorld, with LoCoMo-to-LongMemEval/HotpotQA and cross-model transfer; ALFWorld training uses offline expert trajectories.
papers.limitations: LongMemEval excludes abstention questions and uses validation to tune configurations; ALFWorld includes demonstrations. The system trains controller parameters, so it is not wholly training-free. Benchmark transfer does not establish online lifelong deployment or privacy/access-control guarantees.

papers.title: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution
papers.code_note: Current author repository inspected; it points to a separate mce-artifact repository for paper experiments. Not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Training rollouts and validation utility for candidate context functions and their engineering skills.
papers.mechanism: A meta-agent revises context-engineering skills; a base agent executes them to construct context as files and code. History-informed evolutionary selection retains useful context functions and corresponding skills.
papers.evaluation: Tests finance, chemistry, medicine, law, and safety-classification datasets, with offline and online variants and component ablations.
papers.limitations: Full iterative skill evolution applies to offline experiments; single-pass online processing uses a different variant. The authors identify reasoning-heavy tasks and long, complex trajectories as limitations. Domain tests do not establish clinical or legal validity.

papers.title: Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Proposer–solver feedback grounded in an external search environment.
papers.mechanism: Co-evolves a proposer that generates diverse, challenging questions and a search-enabled solver. Hop-grouped policy optimization shares baselines among structurally similar questions to reduce training overhead.
papers.evaluation: The authors compare the trained search agents with supervised alternatives on several question-answering benchmarks.
papers.limitations: Without training data means without human-annotated task data, not without external information: the search engine supplies a knowledge environment. This abstract-level review does not independently test search freshness, citation fidelity, or long-term robustness.

papers.title: AgentDevel: Reframing Self-Evolving LLM Agents as Release Engineering
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Implementation-blind trace critiques, executable diagnosis, and per-task regression/fix outcomes.
papers.mechanism: Externalizes improvement into a release pipeline that constructs one candidate at a time. Promotion emphasizes which previously passing tasks fail and which failing tasks are repaired.
papers.evaluation: The abstract reports execution-heavy benchmark experiments with fewer regressions and auditable version histories.
papers.limitations: This is an external improvement pipeline rather than in-agent autonomous learning. The abstract review does not establish the benchmark composition, statistical uncertainty, or protection against every regression.

papers.title: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Environment feedback updates the utility assigned to episodic memories.
papers.mechanism: Uses outcome feedback to adjust the utility of episodic memories while keeping the reasoning model fixed. Two-stage retrieval combines semantic relevance with learned utility to select useful past strategies.
papers.evaluation: The authors report results on HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, and Lifelong Agent Bench.
papers.limitations: The abstract and official repository were inspected; training/evaluation separation and statistical uncertainty were not independently audited. Benchmark gains do not settle the stability-plasticity problem in general.

papers.title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents
papers.code_note: Official repository linked from arXiv and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task success and memory-quality rewards, with penalties for redundant storage, tool use, and context growth.
papers.mechanism: Trains an agent to select long-term memory edits and short-term context operations as tools. Three progressive stages and step-wise GRPO assign delayed task rewards to earlier memory decisions; the resulting policy manages external memory during use.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-4B agents on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, PDDL, BabyAI, and HotpotQA, with memory-quality, efficiency, and ablation comparisons.
papers.limitations: The memory-operation vocabulary is fixed. The authors distinguish controlled cross-domain transfer from persistent real-user or long-term dialogue deployments, which remain future evaluation settings.

papers.title: Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models: Decoupling Chosen-Rejected via Past-Future
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Preferences using anchored past-model rejections and newer-model chosen responses.
papers.mechanism: Separates the model generations used to provide rejected and chosen samples so their learning signal does not shrink as both improve together. The paper applies this temporal arrangement to iterative self-rewarding training.
papers.evaluation: The authors compare model families and sizes at matched compute and report instruction-following and selected out-of-distribution reasoning, QA, and coding results.
papers.limitations: This review inspected the proceedings abstract and repository landing page. Curator interpretation: reported task transfer does not establish a calibrated self-judge or unlimited improvement over future generations.

papers.title: PerMemSafe: Benchmarking Implicit Personalized Safety of Long Horizon Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this review; no implementation was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Changing implicit user-risk cues in constructed multi-session conversations, with annotated safety contexts for evaluation.
papers.mechanism: Separates recognizing implicit personalized risks from tracking their changes over time. The accompanying SentinelMem retains explicit fact-state transitions and separates preference information from safety constraints.
papers.evaluation: Compares full-context models and five memory frameworks on safety perception and dynamic evolution, scoring retrieval, personalized response safety, and helpfulness; model grading is checked against a human sample.
papers.limitations: Conversations are synthetic and text-only. Budget limits restrict memory-framework backbones; judge agreement on a sample does not establish reliability for all cases. Response-level scores are not clinical outcomes or evidence of safe autonomous action, and year-only dating avoids inventing a first-public day.

papers.title: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Intervenes on raw and condensed experience to test whether an agent’s decisions causally depend on the experience it receives.
papers.evaluation: Across several frameworks, backbones, and environments, the authors find that condensed experience can be ignored or misinterpreted even when raw experience influences behavior.
papers.limitations: The interventions support conclusions within the tested systems. High end-task scores alone do not reveal whether the intended learning pathway caused a gain.

papers.title: COLLABMEM: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Collaborative Memory Operations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review; no research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Fixed event traces, access/authority labels, and gold probes evaluate memory operations; no policy-learning loop is tested.
papers.mechanism: Holds the interaction trace and answering layer fixed to isolate sharing, access, routing, provenance, conflict resolution, and retention. TMS-GRAPH++ supplies role-filtered views with current-value and writer information.
papers.evaluation: Uses 58 hand-authored seed scenarios plus scaled, adversarial, and compositional probes; compares mechanism reimplementations separately from official SDK memory primitives.
papers.limitations: Controlled traces and minimal sharing policies are not native multi-agent product deployments. Human checking covers a stratified sample; the paper acknowledges that its compression metric inadequately reflects compression capability. Year-only dating preserves the inspected publication precision.

papers.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems
papers.code_note: Paper-linked official repository and EvolveLab README inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task success, token cost, latency, and trajectory diagnoses guide architecture selection and redesign.
papers.mechanism: Searches implementations of encoding, storage, retrieval, and management while each candidate accumulates experience. Pareto selection and a fixed diagnose-and-design operator retain and modify memory architectures inside a supplied interface.
papers.evaluation: Tests GAIA, WebWalkerQA, xBench-DeepSearch, and TaskCraft, including transfer of fixed TaskCraft-evolved architectures across datasets, backbones, and agent frameworks.
papers.limitations: The inspected search uses three outer iterations, fixed selection, and empty candidate memories at each iteration. Pass@1–3 budgets differ across reported rows. Transfer remains within related research/search tasks; evolving a memory interface does not establish improvement of the outer evolution procedure.

papers.title: Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Solver self-consistency, tool-use incentives, diversity penalties, and pseudo-label-based executor rewards.
papers.mechanism: Co-trains a curriculum agent and a tool-using executor in alternating stages. The proposer targets uncertain, diverse tasks, while filtered generated tasks and a code interpreter support executor updates.
papers.evaluation: The paper tests two Qwen base-model sizes on mathematics and general-reasoning suites, comparing tool-enabled baselines and other self-evolving methods.
papers.limitations: No new human-annotated training tasks are required, but pretrained weights, reward design, and tool infrastructure remain inputs. Curator interpretation: majority-derived pseudo-labels need independent correctness checks, and peak training scores are not evidence of indefinite improvement.

papers.title: Live-SWE-agent: Can Software Engineering Agents Self-Evolve on the Fly?
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Runtime observations while solving the current software-engineering problem.
papers.mechanism: Starts with a minimal bash-based agent and permits edits to its own scaffold during task execution. It studies on-the-fly changes to the agent implementation without a separate offline evolution campaign.
papers.evaluation: The authors report software-repair evaluations on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Pro.
papers.limitations: The abstract establishes adaptation during a task, not durable learning carried between independent tasks. Current leaderboard rankings and results from different model versions should not be inferred from the paper.

papers.title: Self-Harmony: Learning to Harmonize Self-Supervision and Self-Play in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository, training instructions, and implementation overview inspected; no installation, model download, or training.
papers.learning_signal: Agreement among model answers to original and reframed questions supplies pseudo-labels, with format/diversity reward terms.
papers.mechanism: One model plays solver and reframer roles, pooling answer frequencies with a harmonic-mean selector. Reinforcement learning updates shared model parameters from original-solution and fused reframe-and-solve trajectories; each benchmark gets its own adapted model.
papers.evaluation: Compares five Qwen/Llama models on six reasoning benchmarks under label-free adaptation, reporting mean pass@1 over multiple rollouts plus pseudo-label, semantic-shift, and component analyses.
papers.limitations: Training uses the same unlabeled questions later scored in evaluation, so results are transductive rather than unseen-task generalization. View agreement is not independent correctness verification, and paraphrases can change meaning. Rollout-count matching does not establish equal total compute; some unstable baselines report peak rather than final scores.

papers.title: OpenSIR: Open-Ended Self-Improving Reasoner
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Difficulty calibration and diversity rewards for self-generated problems.
papers.mechanism: Alternates teacher and student roles within one model, starting from a seed problem. The method rewards exploration of distinct concepts while keeping generated tasks within a learnable difficulty range.
papers.evaluation: The current paper reports mathematical benchmark improvements for instruction and reasoning models and transfer to selected general-reasoning evaluations.
papers.limitations: The paper’s open-ended framing should be read against its finite training runs and benchmark suite. This abstract-level review does not establish correctness of all generated problems or unbounded discovery.

papers.title: SPICE: Self-Play In Corpus Environments Improves Reasoning
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
papers.learning_signal: Document-extracted answers, answer-equivalence checks, and a reward favoring tasks near the solver's capability frontier.
papers.mechanism: A shared model alternates between a document-grounded challenger and a reasoner without document access. Role-specific reinforcement-learning updates improve question generation and solving together.
papers.evaluation: Four Qwen and OctoThinker base models are tested on mathematics and general-reasoning suites, with corpus, task-format, and challenger-reward ablations.
papers.limitations: Experiments use a selected 20,000-document corpus and a fixed training horizon. Curator interpretation: dependence on document quality, generated answers, and verification remains; these experiments do not establish indefinite improvement.

papers.title: Search Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of Agent Capability without Supervision
papers.code_note: Current paper-linked repository and training/service documentation inspected; nothing installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Model-judged answer correctness rewards the solver; solver difficulty rewards the proposer after retrieval-based question filtering.
papers.mechanism: Trains one model in proposer and solver roles. The proposer builds search questions around supplied answers; a retrieval-augmented check filters questions before REINFORCE and GRPO updates retain new behavior in model weights.
papers.evaluation: Reports pass@1 on seven QA benchmarks using local Wikipedia retrieval, including initial training, further training of search-specialized checkpoints, and fixed-opponent and verification ablations.
papers.limitations: Without supervision does not mean without external information: 50,000 seed answers come from public training sets, and Qwen2.5-32B supplies default verification and judgment. Evaluation samples 500 questions per dataset except Bamboogle’s 125. A fixed corpus and ten-call search budget constrain transfer; model verification is not proof of question validity.

papers.title: MARSHAL: Incentivizing Multi-Agent Reasoning via Self-Play with Strategic LLMs
papers.code_note: Official repository, project linkage, and training documentation inspected; no code or checkpoints were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Game outcomes plus engineered action-format and response-length rewards guide online reinforcement learning.
papers.mechanism: Updates one language model through cooperative and competitive self-play. Turn-level returns are centered within player-role groups to assign credit across multi-turn games. The learned weights are then placed in fixed debate or cooperation frameworks.
papers.evaluation: Trains on Tic-Tac-Toe, Kuhn Poker, and Mini Hanabi; evaluates harder held-out games and zero-shot mathematics/QA in MAD and AutoGen. Includes fixed-opponent and credit-assignment ablations, with Qwen3-4B main and 8B extension results.
papers.limitations: Training uses two-player games and designed rewards; it does not evolve the downstream workflow. Hanabi evaluation is self-play, not a test with arbitrary unseen partners. Benefits vary by benchmark and framework; larger populations and practical collaborative software/research environments remain future work.

papers.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Reflection on generated trajectories, execution outcomes, and useful or harmful context entries.
papers.mechanism: Separates generation, reflection, and curation to build an evolving playbook. Small structured updates and deduplication preserve reusable strategies without repeatedly rewriting the entire context.
papers.evaluation: Experiments cover AppWorld and financial-analysis tasks; offline adaptation and sequential predict-then-update evaluation are reported separately.
papers.limitations: Adaptation depends on the reflector extracting useful lessons and can accumulate noise. Online test-stream learning is a different protocol from evaluating a frozen agent on independent tasks.

papers.title: Mem-α: Learning Memory Construction via Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Question-answering accuracy over accumulated interaction history.
papers.mechanism: Trains an agent to construct and update core, episodic, and semantic memory while processing sequential interaction chunks. Rewards come from answering questions over the full interaction history.
papers.evaluation: The authors compare memory-augmented baselines and report generalization from training histories to substantially longer evaluation histories.
papers.limitations: The abstract supports long-context memory construction under a QA objective. Interpretation: longer-context generalization should not be equated with cross-domain procedural learning or autonomous objective selection.

papers.title: Socratic-Zero : Bootstrapping Reasoning via Data-Free Agent Co-evolution
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
papers.learning_signal: A fixed stronger teacher's correctness judgments, reference solutions, and failure-targeted generated problems.
papers.mechanism: Updates a solver through online preference learning and trains a generator to imitate useful teacher-generated curricula. The teacher remains frozen while the solver and generator change.
papers.evaluation: The authors compare solver accuracy on seven mathematical and three general-reasoning benchmarks and assess synthetic data through downstream student training.
papers.limitations: Despite the title, experiments use 100 MATH seed questions, initial supervised tuning on 1,500 problems, and a Qwen3-235B teacher. Mean@32 evaluation and teacher-derived judgments should be preserved when interpreting comparisons; this is not learning without prior data or an external teacher.

papers.title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Self-judged task outcomes and contrasts among multiple execution trajectories.
papers.mechanism: Extracts reusable reasoning lessons from self-judged successful and failed trajectories and retrieves them for later tasks. Memory-aware test-time scaling adds diverse attempts to improve the experience available for consolidation.
papers.evaluation: The study evaluates sequential web-browsing and software-engineering tasks, with memory baselines, failure-trajectory ablations, and test-time-compute comparisons.
papers.limitations: The learning signal relies on model judgments rather than access to ground truth during the task stream. Interpretation: memory gains should be compared under matched compute budgets, task order, and protection against retrieving the current task’s answer.

papers.title: A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework for LLM-Based Agent Memory
papers.code_note: Author-linked repository and README inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Divergence among reasoning paths generated from retrieved memories and detected anomalous paths retained as lessons.
papers.mechanism: Validates retrieved memories through parallel reasoning-path comparisons and keeps detected failure patterns in a separate lesson store. Later actions consult those lessons without changing the core agent architecture.
papers.evaluation: Reports direct and indirect memory-poisoning tests with ReAct-StrategyQA, EHRAgent, and WebShop, two backbones, retrieval variants, benign-task utility, and collaborative-agent extensions.
papers.limitations: The threat model assumes mostly benign memory and limited attacker control. The abstract’s over-95% reduction should not be read as uniform end-to-end protection: Table 1 retains substantial task-level attack success despite strong retrieval-stage suppression. Consensus and lesson extraction remain model-dependent.

papers.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Downstream answer outcomes used for PPO and GRPO training.
papers.mechanism: Trains a memory-management agent to add, update, delete, or retain entries, alongside an answer agent that selects and uses relevant memories. Outcome-driven reinforcement learning updates the policies governing external memory.
papers.evaluation: The current abstract reports evaluation on LoCoMo, MSC, and LongMemEval across several model scales and question types.
papers.limitations: Evidence reviewed here is the current abstract, not an audit of the training split or reward implementation. Conversation-memory QA gains do not establish improvement on long-horizon tool-use tasks.

papers.title: Building Self-Evolving Agents via Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning: A Framework and Benchmark
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Benchmark task success, long-term retention through environmental tools, and proactive initiative metrics.

Its framework is a research agenda and evaluation setting rather than a single demonstrated learning algorithm.
papers.evaluation: The inspected preprint v6 resets agent context between tasks; retained information must be explicitly stored and retrieved through environmental tools such as calendars and drafts. The later published abstract additionally describes context-engineering comparisons, whose full protocol was not reviewed here.
papers.limitations: The selected full-text review concerns the preprint v6 baseline in a designed simulation, not a trained lifelong learner’s learning curve. The renamed Findings of EMNLP 2026 version has verified publication metadata; its full experimental revision was not inspected.

papers.title: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
papers.code_note: The author-linked Agent-on-the-Fly repository redirects to Memento-Teams/Memento; public page inspected, not executed.

papers.limitations: Validation Pass@3 and test accuracy use different protocols. The parametric variant performs gradient updates outside the LLM, so the whole system should not be described as parameter-free. Long-horizon Level 3 tasks remain difficult.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Describes an evolution loop through inputs, agent systems, environments, and optimizers, then maps techniques and domain-specific applications onto those components.
papers.evaluation: Reviews methods alongside evaluation, safety, and ethical considerations.
papers.limitations: Review coverage and categories reflect the authors’ literature selection; the framework does not itself demonstrate lifelong capability growth.

papers.title: Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.

papers.mechanism: Distills trajectories into both detailed instructions and more abstract procedures. Its procedural-memory pipeline builds, retrieves, revises, and retires entries as further experience arrives.
papers.evaluation: The paper studies TravelPlanner and ALFWorld and reports transfer of procedural memory from a stronger model to a weaker one.

papers.title: R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data

papers.evaluation: The authors report mathematical and general-domain reasoning improvements across multiple backbone models.
papers.limitations: The framework still depends on pretrained models and the designed reward procedure. This abstract-level review does not independently validate generated task correctness, long-run stability, or open-world transfer.

papers.title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.

papers.evaluation: Synthesizes published methods, benchmarks, and open questions rather than evaluating one new learner.

papers.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.

papers.evaluation: The final proceedings abstract reports comparisons with GRPO and MIPROv2 across six tasks, plus inference-time code optimization.
papers.limitations: The headline comparison concerns the reported models, tasks, and budgets; it is not a general ranking of prompt optimization and reinforcement learning. Curator interpretation: total evaluation and reflector costs matter alongside rollout counts.

papers.title: EvoAgentX: An Automated Framework for Evolving Agentic Workflows

papers.learning_signal: Task evaluations used by integrated prompt and workflow optimizers.
papers.mechanism: Integrates workflow generation and execution with optimization methods including TextGrad, AFlow, and MIPRO. The framework supports changes to prompts, tool configurations, and workflow topology.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate QA, coding, and math workflows on HotpotQA, MBPP, and MATH, with additional GAIA tasks.

papers.title: SPIRAL: Self-Play on Zero-Sum Games Incentivizes Reasoning via Multi-Agent Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
papers.learning_signal: Terminal game outcomes and role-conditioned advantage estimates.
papers.mechanism: One shared language-model policy plays both sides of zero-sum games and receives online policy-gradient updates. Separate baselines for each role stabilize training as the opposing policy improves.
papers.evaluation: The study trains on TicTacToe, Kuhn Poker, and Simple Negotiation and evaluates transfer to mathematical and general reasoning benchmarks across several Qwen and Llama configurations.
papers.limitations: The curriculum depends on engineered games and pretrained models. The authors report substantial compute, training plateaus, and limited academic-benchmark transfer evidence; game rewards can favor strategies other than the intended reasoning skill.

papers.title: Self-Adapting Language Models
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.

papers.evaluation: Experiments cover knowledge incorporation and few-shot ARC adaptation; the paper also tests retention after sequential knowledge edits.

papers.title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.code_note: Author-linked public repository page inspected; not executed.

papers.evaluation: Reports five benchmarks spanning embodied action, knowledge QA, and games, using three language-model backbones and three multi-agent frameworks, alongside cost and component analyses.
papers.limitations: This changes the memory supplied to existing teams; it does not establish autonomous redesign of their coordination or models. The authors leave broader domain validation, including medical QA, for future work.

papers.title: Self-Challenging Language Model Agents
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Self-generated task verification functions and tests, followed by task-evaluation rewards.
papers.mechanism: The agent first explores supplied tools as a challenger and constructs Code-as-Task problems containing instructions, a verifier, and passing and failing examples. It then learns as an executor through reinforcement learning on the filtered generated tasks.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate multi-turn tool use on M3ToolEval and TauBench.
papers.limitations: Tool interfaces and the learning framework are supplied externally. Curator interpretation: tests of a generated verifier cannot establish that every generated task captures its intended semantics or that gains transfer to arbitrary tools.

papers.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Coding-benchmark outcomes and evaluation logs used to propose self-edits.
papers.mechanism: A coding agent rewrites its own implementation, and an archive retains runnable variants as possible parents for later edits. This permits exploration beyond the latest or immediately best-performing agent.
papers.evaluation: The paper evaluates SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot subsets, ablates self-improvement and archive exploration, and studies transfer across foundation models.
papers.limitations: Foundation models, archive management, and parent selection remain fixed in the inspected study. Staged search and evaluation use benchmark subsets, so the reported curves should not be interpreted as a fully separate hidden-task deployment evaluation.

papers.title: LifelongAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Experience from earlier interactive tasks.
papers.mechanism: Constructs interdependent tasks grounded in reusable skills across database, operating-system, and knowledge-graph environments.
papers.evaluation: Tests experience reuse and a group self-consistency mechanism; ordinary replay is limited by irrelevant context and context length.
papers.limitations: Performance on these task sequences should be separated from general lifelong learning. The abstract does not establish a complete audit of forgetting or long-term deployment.

papers.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Executable task validity, solution correctness, and task learnability rewards.
papers.mechanism: A single model proposes and solves code-based tasks, with a code executor validating problems and answers. Reinforcement learning updates both roles while the generated task buffer supplies a changing curriculum.
papers.evaluation: Experiments compare coding and mathematics reasoning across base-model families and scales, with ablations of task types and proposer design.
papers.limitations: Zero data refers to new task and answer supervision during this training stage; the system starts from pretrained models and uses an engineered executor and task format. Curator interpretation: bounded benchmark gains do not establish unlimited improvement.

papers.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Ongoing conversations and model-mediated fact extraction and consolidation.
papers.mechanism: Extracts and consolidates facts from conversations for later retrieval, with a graph variant for relational information. Persistent conversational state provides a useful comparison point for more explicit experience-learning methods.
papers.evaluation: The paper compares memory systems, retrieval approaches, and full-context baselines on LoCoMo using answer-quality, latency, and token-cost measures.
papers.limitations: The reported evaluation concerns conversational recall and QA. The title’s production-readiness wording is an author characterization; this review does not establish deployment reliability or procedural self-improvement.

papers.title: RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
papers.learning_signal: Environment rewards on multi-turn trajectories, with reward variability and gradient diagnostics guiding stabilization.
papers.mechanism: StarPO optimizes reasoning-action trajectories with reinforcement learning. The study identifies repetitive reasoning collapse and tests StarPO-S interventions including rollout filtering, a critic, and gradient stabilization.
papers.evaluation: Version 2 studies Bandit, Sokoban, FrozenLake, and WebShop, varying optimization, rollout design, rewards, and generalization conditions.
papers.limitations: The paper reports small-scale tasks and no multimodal evaluation. Better rewards do not guarantee meaningful reasoning. The linked repository now includes RAGEN-2 and additional environments; its current branch is not a pinned reproduction of this paper.

papers.title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
papers.code_note: Official repository linked in the paper and landing page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Benchmark feedback and LLM reflection on candidate code changes.
papers.mechanism: Equips a coding agent with tools to edit its own implementation and reuses improved versions in later iterations. Learning changes the surrounding agent code rather than model parameters.
papers.evaluation: The paper reports gains on a random SWE-bench Verified subset, LiveCodeBench, and synthetic agent tasks.
papers.limitations: The software-repair result uses a fixed 50-task subset and a five-minute timeout. The authors note that faster file editing explains part of the gain, with limited improvements on reasoning tasks; repeated benchmark evaluation is distinct from held-out deployment transfer.

papers.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Official system repository inspected; it distinguishes this reusable memory package from the separate paper-evaluation repository. Neither was executed.
papers.learning_signal: New observations and language-model judgments of relationships among notes.
papers.mechanism: Constructs structured notes, links related memories, and updates older contextual descriptions when new information arrives. The evolving note network changes retrieval context without modifying model weights.
papers.evaluation: The primary abstract reports comparisons with memory baselines across six foundation models.
papers.limitations: This review covers the abstract and official memory-system page. Interpretation: reorganizing a memory store is a form of adaptation, but it is not sufficient evidence of growing procedural skill or reliable long-term retention.

papers.title: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
papers.learning_signal: Environment terminal rewards, tree-search alternatives, and actor-selected error locations.
papers.mechanism: Uses Monte Carlo tree search to pair unsuccessful and successful paths. The current actor selects a revision point, and spliced correction trajectories support iterative supervised training of an error-recovery policy.
papers.evaluation: The authors test three training iterations on WebShop, ScienceWorld, and TextCraft, comparing task reward, recovery from truncated failures, and action-loop behavior.
papers.limitations: Training also uses ShareGPT data and manually written revision connectors. The evaluated setup uses a specific backbone and reward-bearing environments; learning to revise a trajectory is distinct from modifying the learning algorithm.

papers.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Tests information extraction, cross-session and temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention from long interaction histories, separating indexing, retrieval, and reading.
papers.evaluation: Evaluates memory designs and downstream question answering over controlled histories with scalable length.
papers.limitations: Recall and evidence use are components of learning agents, not direct proof of procedural improvement. History version, reader, retrieval budget, and grader must be matched for comparisons.

papers.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Execution scores on a validation subset and stored search experience.
papers.mechanism: Searches over code-represented workflows using a Monte Carlo tree-search variant. An LLM changes prompts and connections between operations, while the tree retains feedback from prior candidates.
papers.evaluation: Six QA, coding, and math datasets are divided into development and test subsets; the paper also compares execution costs and transfer between executor models.
papers.limitations: The study focuses on reasoning tasks with accessible evaluators and commonly used operators. Search costs and repeated validation exposure should be considered separately from the inference cost of the selected workflow.

papers.title: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Task scores and an in-context performance predictor used to screen candidates.
papers.mechanism: Defines interchangeable planning, reasoning, tool-use, and memory modules, then searches by evolving and recombining them. A performance predictor reduces evaluations of unpromising designs.
papers.evaluation: The authors compare generated agents on six benchmarks spanning web, embodied, tool-use, and game tasks.
papers.limitations: Optimization operates within predefined module interfaces and an external search framework. Curator interpretation: gains under these tasks do not establish unrestricted architectural invention or continual learning after deployment.

papers.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: High-level objectives and task-performance feedback.
papers.mechanism: Lets an LLM-based agent inspect and revise its own logic through a self-referential learning framework. The editable artifact is the agent program rather than the underlying language-model weights.
papers.evaluation: The paper reports experiments in mathematical reasoning and agent tasks, with performance, efficiency, and generalization comparisons.
papers.limitations: Empirical task gains are not formal proofs that a modification is beneficial. The ACL proceedings title uses Recursively Self-Improvement; it is the same research lineage as the linked arXiv record.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Online rewards and regularization over self-generated multi-turn correction traces.
papers.mechanism: Trains a correction policy on its own response distribution, with an initialization stage and a reward bonus encouraging successful revision. The method targets distribution mismatch and collapsed correction behavior observed in offline supervised training.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate self-correction on MATH and HumanEval using Gemini models.

papers.title: Agent Workflow Memory

papers.learning_signal: Annotated offline trajectories or model-judged successful online task trajectories.
papers.mechanism: Abstracts reusable subroutines from action trajectories and adds them to the agent context as workflow memory. It supports an offline store built from training examples and an online store updated after completed tasks.

papers.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems

papers.mechanism: A meta-agent writes new agent programs, evaluates them, and uses the growing archive to propose further designs. Code represents the prompts, control flow, and other components being searched.
papers.evaluation: Experiments cover coding, science, and math, with reported transfer of discovered designs across tasks and models.
