papers.title: Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Answer correctness and improved responses from self-distillation or a stronger teacher.
papers.mechanism: Turns single-turn problems into multi-turn trajectories and trains the model to revise earlier unsuccessful responses. Its training loop uses reward-weighted supervised learning over the current model’s attempts and improved continuations.
papers.evaluation: Math-reasoning experiments compare sequential improvement with single-turn strategies under comparable inference budgets and examine iterative training and distribution shift.
papers.limitations: The learned correction policy persists in weights, while the revisions at deployment concern the current problem. Some data-collection variants use a stronger model; this is not recursive modification of the learning algorithm itself.

papers.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Recursive resampling and training on prior-generation model outputs.
papers.mechanism: Analyzes how repeated training on generated data can lose low-probability parts of an original distribution and amplify errors. The paper combines tractable distribution models with generative-model experiments.
papers.evaluation: Experiments include Gaussian mixtures, variational autoencoders, and repeated language-model fine-tuning, with differing amounts of original data retained.
papers.limitations: The theoretical replacement setting and finite experiments have specific data-mixing assumptions. Curator interpretation: this is a warning about recursive data use, not a proof that every verified or data-accumulating self-learning loop must fail.

papers.title: Symbolic Learning Enables Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Natural-language representations of losses and gradients derived from task outcomes.
papers.mechanism: Represents an agent as a symbolic network whose editable components include prompts, tools, and their composition. Symbolic optimization uses textual feedback to revise that network.
papers.evaluation: The abstract describes proof-of-concept experiments on standard benchmarks and more complex tasks.
papers.limitations: These are natural-language analogues of gradient-based learning, not mathematical derivatives of a differentiable objective. The reviewed abstract does not establish unrestricted long-term learning after deployment.

papers.title: TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text
papers.venue: Nature 2025; journal title: Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Natural-language critiques propagated through a computation graph.
papers.mechanism: Treats components of a compound AI system as editable variables and routes textual feedback backward to propose updates. Applications include reusable prompt optimization and refinement of individual outputs.
papers.evaluation: The paper reports studies in question answering, code generation, molecule design, and treatment-plan optimization.
papers.limitations: Output refinement and reusable system learning are different experimental settings. Curator interpretation: success under an LLM critic does not by itself establish correctness or clinical validity.

papers.title: ReST-MCTS*: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Known final answers and search-derived estimates of intermediate-step value.
papers.mechanism: Combines process-reward-guided tree search with iterative training of the policy and reward models. Search supplies reasoning traces and step-value targets without requiring human labels for every intermediate step.
papers.evaluation: The authors compare search methods at matched search budgets and report multi-iteration self-training results for three language models.
papers.limitations: Oracle final answers remain available, and inferred step rewards depend on the search procedure. Curator interpretation: removing manual process labels does not remove external supervision.

papers.title: Re-ReST: Reflection-Reinforced Self-Training for Language Agents
papers.code_note: Official repository page inspected; no installation, training, or result reproduction performed.
papers.learning_signal: External training-time feedback such as answer correctness, environment outcomes, and unit tests.
papers.mechanism: Trains a separate reflector to repair unsuccessful model-generated examples. Accepted original and repaired trajectories then fine-tune the agent, so improvement is retained in its parameters; the main inference path needs only the trained agent.
papers.evaluation: Experiments cover multi-hop question answering, ALFWorld, code generation, visual question answering, and image generation, with reflector and preference-training analyses.
papers.limitations: Feedback and task inputs are supplied during training. The reflector shares the model family but not weights with the agent. A separate self-consistency inference variant should not be confused with the main training-only use of reflection.

papers.title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Repeated generated-data training with old data retained rather than replaced.
papers.mechanism: Compares replacement of earlier datasets with accumulation of original and synthetic data. It supplies a linear-model analysis and generative-model experiments showing that the data-retention policy changes collapse behavior.
papers.evaluation: The study includes small transformer language models on TinyStories, molecular diffusion, image variational autoencoders, and controlled analytical models.
papers.limitations: The bounded-error theorem is for its stated linear setting, and retaining growing datasets changes resource requirements. Curator interpretation: these results challenge universal collapse claims without certifying arbitrary self-training or agent-memory loops.

papers.title: TroVE: Inducing Verifiable and Efficient Toolboxes for Solving Programmatic Tasks
papers.code_note: Official repository linked by the paper and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Agreement among executed candidate outputs, program simplicity, and observed tool reuse.
papers.mechanism: Samples solutions that import existing functions, create new ones, or use only supplied primitives. Execution agreement and simplicity select a solution whose functions join a reusable toolbox; periodic trimming removes low-use functions without model training.
papers.evaluation: Tests 11 math, table-QA, and visual-reasoning datasets. A separate study asks six people to verify 100 table-QA solutions and measures verification time and accuracy.
papers.limitations: Supplied primitives and demonstrations constrain the tool space. Agreement is not proof of correctness, and the human study does not establish universal reliability. Some comparisons reuse previously reported baseline scores.

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: The language model judges candidate responses to construct preferences for iterative DPO.
papers.mechanism: Uses one language model both to answer instructions and to score responses, updating it through successive rounds of preference optimization. This couples the response generator and the source of training rewards.
papers.evaluation: The paper reports instruction-following and reward-quality improvements across three iterations, including AlpacaEval 2.0 evaluation.
papers.limitations: The evidence concerns bounded iterations and selected evaluation protocols. Curator interpretation: agreement with an evolving self-judge is not an independent guarantee of correctness or indefinite improvement.

papers.title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Contrasts previous-model responses with existing human demonstrations.
papers.mechanism: Starts with a supervised model and iteratively learns to distinguish its own generated responses from reference demonstrations. Successive model versions provide the changing opponent in the training objective.
papers.evaluation: The authors report results on Open LLM Leaderboard tasks, MT-Bench, and Big-Bench datasets.
papers.limitations: No additional human annotation is required by the loop, but existing human demonstrations remain its target distribution. Curator interpretation: this is not learning from zero prior human data.

papers.title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Separates self-correction questions by feedback source and training assumptions, and examines whether experimental designs support the claimed correction ability.
papers.evaluation: The reviewed evidence favors reliable external feedback or trained correction in many settings, while questioning broad claims for prompted intrinsic correction.
papers.limitations: This is a review of the literature available in 2024, not a universal impossibility theorem or a measurement of current models.

papers.title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Builds extended conversations from persona and event structures, with human editing, to test recall, event summarization, and multimodal dialogue.
papers.evaluation: Compares memory approaches on the LoCoMo conversational benchmark.
papers.limitations: Recall from generated and edited conversations differs from learning a reusable procedure or improving an agent. Dataset statistics differ between paper and project versions; pin the artifact before comparing scores.

papers.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Tests intrinsic correction: asking a model to revise its own reasoning using no external correctness signal.
papers.evaluation: The studied reasoning settings show weak correction and, in some cases, degradation after revision.
papers.limitations: The result concerns the tested models, prompts, and tasks; it does not rule out externally grounded feedback, learned correction, or durable agent learning.

papers.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Interaction history and agent-selected memory operations.
papers.mechanism: Lets a language-model agent move information between a limited active context and external memory tiers through explicit operations. This supplies persistent state and self-managed context for later interactions.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate document analysis beyond the active context window and memory across multiple chat sessions.
papers.limitations: This is an adjacent memory architecture: remembered facts and context management do not alone establish accumulation of reusable task competence. Current software descended from the research may differ from the evaluated version.

papers.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: A developer-specified metric and examples used to bootstrap demonstrations.
papers.mechanism: Represents language-model pipelines as declarative modules and compiles demonstrations for their component prompts. The reusable artifact is an optimized pipeline configuration.
papers.evaluation: The paper studies math reasoning and retrieval-based question-answering pipelines, comparing compiled programs with hand-written prompts and demonstrations.
papers.limitations: Compilation is externally configured optimization; the paper does not establish an agent that autonomously maintains learning after deployment. The proceedings landing page uses a title variant ending in State-of-the-Art Pipelines.

papers.title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Utility functions scoring the programs produced by an improver.
papers.mechanism: Begins with an LLM-assisted program improver and applies that improver to its own source. Candidate improvers are assessed through the quality of programs they generate for downstream tasks.
papers.evaluation: The study reports improvements on a small set of algorithmic tasks and separately examines attempts to bypass a sandbox.
papers.limitations: The authors explicitly retain a fixed language model, so the result is bounded scaffold self-improvement. Performance on the small task set does not establish an indefinitely accelerating process.

papers.title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Fitness on task examples guides selection of task prompts and mutation prompts.
papers.mechanism: Evolves a population of task instructions together with the instructions that produce their mutations. It provides a concrete example of changing part of the improvement procedure as well as the task-solving prompt.
papers.evaluation: Evaluations cover arithmetic, commonsense reasoning, and hate-speech classification.
papers.limitations: The foundation model and surrounding evolutionary procedure remain fixed. Prompt-level self-reference should not be read as evidence of unbounded improvement of the complete agent.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Optimizers
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Scores of earlier candidate prompts on a development task.
papers.mechanism: Uses an LLM to propose candidates from a history of instructions and their measured scores. Selected instructions can be reused on new examples without changing model weights.
papers.evaluation: Prompt optimization is evaluated on GSM8K and BIG-Bench Hard, alongside illustrative numerical and combinatorial optimization tasks.
papers.limitations: This is an external prompt-search procedure, not evidence of autonomous lifelong agent learning. Curator interpretation: the chosen objective and development data constrain what the search can improve.

papers.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task outcomes and model-generated comparisons of successful and unsuccessful trajectories.
papers.mechanism: Collects training-task trajectories, contrasts successes and failures to extract reusable textual insights, and retrieves relevant experiences for new tasks. Learning changes the external experience and insight stores without updating the base model.
papers.evaluation: The paper evaluates HotpotQA, ALFWorld, and WebShop, examines insight and retrieval ablations, and studies transfer from question answering to fact verification.
papers.limitations: The investigated environments have textual observations and are deterministic. The authors note that larger lifelong insight stores would need additional retrieval beyond fitting all insights into context.

papers.title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: A reward-based training objective applied to batches sampled from the current policy.
papers.mechanism: Alternates generating a batch of candidate outputs and improving the policy with offline reinforcement learning. Reusing generated data reduces the need to sample a new online batch for every update.
papers.evaluation: The reported experiments focus on machine translation, assessed using automatic metrics and human evaluation.
papers.limitations: This is externally organized model training on a specific application. Curator interpretation: the study does not establish a lifelong agent or a reward signal that itself improves without outside specification.

papers.title: RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent for Robotic Manipulation
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not established in this review; no installation, training, or research execution was performed.
papers.learning_signal: Human demonstrations, goal-relabeled robot trajectories, and learned success detectors used during data collection.
papers.mechanism: Fine-tunes a visual goal-conditioned generalist into task-specific policies, collects additional trajectories with them, then retrains a generalist on old and new data. Reusable improvement resides in model weights rather than an expanding executable skill library.
papers.evaluation: Reports simulation and real-robot manipulation across embodiments, adaptation to new tasks, and an isolated comparison of demonstrations alone versus demonstrations plus self-generated data.
papers.limitations: The reported loop demonstrates one successful iteration and uses 100–1000 teleoperated demonstrations per new task. Humans start and stop collection; robot policies stay frozen during physical interaction. Controlled laboratory backgrounds and imperfect success detectors limit generalization and safety claims.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Tool Makers
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task examples and feedback from producing and using generated tools.
papers.mechanism: Separates tool creation from tool use, allowing a stronger model to create reusable programs that a cheaper model can invoke on related requests. A functional cache retains these capabilities across requests.
papers.evaluation: The paper compares task accuracy and serving cost on reasoning problems, including BIG-Bench tasks.
papers.limitations: Results depend on the selected task families and how tool-making costs are amortized. Interpretation: reusable tool creation does not establish unrestricted autonomous software evolution.

papers.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Environment observations, interpreter errors, and model-based task verification.
papers.mechanism: Builds an expanding library of executable Minecraft skills, retrieved and composed for later tasks. An automatic curriculum proposes objectives, while execution feedback and a model-based critic guide program repair before a skill is retained.
papers.evaluation: The authors compare exploration, technology-tree progress, ablations, and reuse of learned skills on new tasks in another Minecraft world.
papers.limitations: Results concern a simulator with supplied control APIs. The paper reports inaccurate self-verification and impossible proposed tasks, so its retained library is not guaranteed correct.

papers.title: CREATOR: Tool Creation for Disentangling Abstract and Concrete Reasoning of Large Language Models
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Problem specifications and execution feedback for tool creation and revision.
papers.mechanism: Decomposes problem solving into tool design, implementation, execution, and revision so an agent can create tools beyond a fixed API inventory. It also examines reuse of created tools for knowledge transfer.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate MATH, TabMWP, and the introduced Creation Challenge dataset, with tool-use and reasoning baselines.
papers.limitations: Much of the framework concerns solving and repairing an individual problem. Interpretation: tool-transfer experiments should be separated from claims of a continually improving cross-task agent.

papers.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Past interactions, elapsed time, and assigned memory importance.
papers.mechanism: Maintains retrievable interaction memories and user summaries, with time- and importance-sensitive forgetting and reinforcement. The SiliconFriend application combines this memory mechanism with a separately tuned conversational model.
papers.evaluation: The paper combines qualitative user-dialogue analysis with quantitative tests on model-generated long-term conversations.
papers.limitations: Simulated dialogue and personalization outcomes are not clinical validation or evidence of general task-skill improvement. The memory mechanism should be distinguished from separate model tuning.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.code_note: Official repository inspected; not executed. The ACM record was inaccessible during this review, so the catalog status conservatively describes the inspected preprint.
papers.learning_signal: Observed simulated events and model-generated reflections.
papers.mechanism: Stores experiences, synthesizes higher-level reflections, and retrieves relevant memories to plan behavior in a simulated town. The accumulated state shapes subsequent actions and social interactions.
papers.evaluation: The authors assess behavioral believability and emergent coordination in a sandbox populated by simulated agents, including architecture ablations.
papers.limitations: Believability is a different outcome from task competence or factual correctness. This is an adjacent foundation for persistent reflective memory, not a demonstration of open-ended capability improvement.

papers.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Model-generated feedback on the current answer.
papers.mechanism: Uses the same language model to draft, critique, and revise an answer iteratively without updating model weights.
papers.evaluation: The paper compares iterative refinement with one-shot generation on several generation and reasoning tasks using human and automatic assessments.
papers.limitations: These are within-task output improvements. They do not establish retained learning on later tasks, and the evaluation conditions differ from studies of intrinsic reasoning correction.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Scalar or textual environment feedback, exact-match grading, heuristics, and model-generated evaluation, depending on the experiment.
papers.mechanism: Converts task feedback into verbal reflections and carries those reflections into later attempts through an episodic memory buffer. The underlying language-model weights stay fixed.
papers.evaluation: The study evaluates repeated attempts on ALFWorld, HotpotQA, and programming tasks, with ablations of reflection and feedback.
papers.limitations: The central experiments improve retries of the same task; they do not establish a durable cross-task learning library. Feedback sources differ by task, and the paper uses bounded memory.

papers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Self-supervised tool-use examples seeded by a small number of demonstrations for each API.
papers.mechanism: Teaches a language model when to call a predefined API, which arguments to produce, and how to incorporate the returned information. The learned capability is stored in model parameters rather than a growing tool library.
papers.evaluation: The paper evaluates zero-shot downstream tasks using tools such as a calculator, question answering, search, translation, and a calendar.
papers.limitations: The available APIs and initial demonstrations are supplied by researchers. Curator interpretation: learning to invoke these tools is distinct from autonomously creating new tools or learning continually after deployment.

papers.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Model-generated instruction/input/output examples filtered for invalidity and similarity.
papers.mechanism: Bootstraps an instruction-tuning dataset from the model, filters unsuitable examples, and fine-tunes the original model on the retained data. It is a foundation for synthetic-data learning rather than a deployed agent that learns during use.
papers.evaluation: The paper evaluates instruction following on Super-NaturalInstructions and expert-written novel tasks, including human assessment.
papers.limitations: The generator inherits its pretrained capabilities and biases, and dataset filtering is part of the learning system. Curator interpretation: better instruction following alone is not evidence of continual agent learning.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Human-authored principles guide AI critiques, revisions, and preference judgments.
papers.mechanism: Uses self-critiques and revisions for supervised learning, then learns a preference model from AI comparisons and optimizes the assistant with reinforcement learning. The process automates parts of supervision while retaining an externally chosen constitution.
papers.evaluation: The authors report human evaluations of helpfulness and harmlessness for trained assistants.
papers.limitations: The constitution and training procedure are designed externally. Curator interpretation: this supports AI-assisted alignment training, not unsupervised value discovery or a guarantee that safety persists through later self-modification.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Environment observations during task execution.
papers.mechanism: Interleaves reasoning traces with actions and observations so a language model can gather information and revise its plan during a task.
papers.evaluation: Experiments cover question answering, fact verification, ALFWorld, and WebShop with comparisons to reasoning-only and acting-only approaches.
papers.limitations: Included as a baseline agent loop. The prompted interaction loop does not itself establish persistent self-learning between tasks.

papers.title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Known correct answers filter generated rationales; answer hints support rationalization of failed examples.
papers.mechanism: Generates reasoning traces, keeps traces ending in the reference answer, and fine-tunes on them. Failed problems can be retried with the answer supplied as a hint; each outer iteration retrains from the original base model on the newly collected traces.
papers.evaluation: Experiments cover arithmetic, CommonsenseQA, and GSM8K, with comparisons to direct-answer fine-tuning and prompted reasoning.
papers.limitations: The method needs training questions, reference answers, and a small rationale seed. Correct final answers do not independently certify that every intermediate explanation is valid.

papers.title: Mastering the game of Go without human knowledge
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Game outcomes and search-improved move selections from self-play.
papers.mechanism: Trains a policy/value network on games generated by its own search, then uses the updated network to improve subsequent search and play. This is an early concrete example of a coupled data-generation and policy-improvement loop.
papers.evaluation: The authors evaluate playing strength against earlier Go programs, including the previously published champion-defeating AlphaGo.
papers.limitations: The environment supplies exact rules, legal moves, and a reliable win/loss signal. Curator interpretation: success in this closed game does not establish open-ended language-agent learning.

systems.name: A-MEM memory system
systems.relationship_note: The authors distinguish this reusable memory-system repository from the separate AgenticMemory repository used for paper-result reproduction.
systems.learning_signal: New memory content, model-generated context/tags, and similarity to existing notes.
systems.mechanism: Builds structured memory notes, indexes them in ChromaDB, and links or revises related memories as new information arrives. This adapts the external memory organization.
systems.evaluation: The README refers to paper comparisons but directs reproduction work to a different evaluation repository.
systems.limitations: Current library functionality is not proof that the paper’s evaluation has been reproduced. The agent and persistent-memory policy still need application-specific integration.
systems.availability_note: Public reusable memory-library source; package installation documented; not installed or run.
systems.requirements: Python dependencies, ChromaDB/embedding support, and an OpenAI, Ollama, SGLang, or OpenRouter backend as documented.

systems.name: Absolute Zero Reasoner
systems.relationship_note: Official Absolute Zero Reasoner release. The README points to a separate paper branch for original-result replication; the moving development code should not be assumed equivalent.
systems.learning_signal: Python execution validates generated tasks and answers and supplies proposer/solver rewards.
systems.mechanism: Implements reinforced self-play in which a model proposes reasoning tasks and solves them with execution-based verification. Updated weights and a generated task pool support later training iterations.
capabilities: Generate and validate code-based reasoning tasks
Use linked evaluation code, checkpoints, and experiment logs
systems.evaluation: The paper reports coding and mathematics benchmarks; the repository provides training/evaluation resources and distinguishes its paper branch. No checkpoint or training run was tested here.
systems.limitations: The README labels newer development changes as under testing and the raw executor as research-only. Zero newly curated task data does not remove pretraining or engineered supervision.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: GPU training environment with veRL and pretrained weights; documented model-size configurations use multiple 80 GB GPUs. A sandbox executor option requires Docker.

systems.name: ADAS / Meta Agent Search
systems.relationship_note: Official research implementation of Automated Design of Agentic Systems and its Meta Agent Search algorithm; benchmark folders contain separate experiment setups.
systems.learning_signal: Benchmark evaluation and an archive of previously generated agent designs.
systems.mechanism: A fixed meta-agent search procedure writes candidate agent programs, evaluates them, and consults earlier discoveries when proposing new designs. Domain-specific evaluators determine which designs are useful.
capabilities: Retain evaluated discoveries in an archive
Adapt domain-specific search and scoring functions
systems.evaluation: The paper reports task and model transfer experiments; the repository documents how to run the domain studies. No search run was executed here.
systems.limitations: The search procedure is externally configured rather than itself established as an evolving optimizer. The repository explicitly notes that it executes model-generated code.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Python 3.11 environment, required dependencies, model access, and the selected domain’s data and evaluation setup.

systems.name: AFlow
systems.relationship_note: Official standalone AFlow repository, migrated from MetaGPT; it implements the workflow-search method associated with the paper.
systems.learning_signal: Validation-set execution scores and retained search history.
systems.mechanism: Searches code-represented workflows using a Monte Carlo tree-search variant over configurable operators. An evaluator scores candidate workflows and guides later prompt and structure changes.
capabilities: Inspect released workflow and validation traces
systems.evaluation: The project provides evaluation code and experiment artifacts for QA, coding, and mathematics tasks; the collection has not rerun them.
systems.limitations: The README warns that some operators may contain migration bugs. Repeated validation use and search cost must be separated from the selected workflow’s test performance and inference cost.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Documented Python 3.9 environment, model configuration, benchmark data, and task operators/evaluator.

systems.name: Agent Lightning v1.0
systems.relationship_note: Official Microsoft agent-training framework. Its v1.0 technical report is linked by the project but is not yet a separate literature entry in this catalog; legacy v0.x is maintained on another branch.
systems.learning_signal: Task rewards and trajectories collected from agents running their existing harnesses.
systems.mechanism: Separates policy training, model-request interception, and agent rollout execution through a trainer, API gateway, and controller. Captured interactions become training samples while the agent retains its tool and control-flow environment.
capabilities: Train policies using real agent harnesses
Collect model interactions through an API gateway
Run rollouts locally or as Kubernetes jobs
systems.evaluation: Project documentation reports search, sandbox, and coding-agent examples. These are project-reported results, not measurements performed or reproduced by this collection.
systems.limitations: This is externally configured training infrastructure, not proof of autonomous self-directed improvement. The v1.0 architecture is a documented refactor, so v0.x installation and experiment assumptions should not be transferred automatically.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: NVIDIA CUDA and a compatible verl/vLLM/PyTorch training stack; current setup docs describe W&B logging and local or Kubernetes rollout environments.

systems.name: Agent Workflow Memory
systems.relationship_note: Author implementation of AWM, with separate Mind2Web and WebArena pipelines.
systems.learning_signal: Annotated training examples in offline mode, or prior action trajectories in online mode.
systems.mechanism: Induces reusable workflow descriptions from example trajectories and supplies them through agent memory. Offline and online pipelines make the source of experience explicit.
systems.evaluation: The README reports web-task results; inspected subdirectory instructions show the offline and online execution paths.
systems.limitations: Web task environments and data must be provisioned separately. The online and offline protocols should not be treated as interchangeable learning evidence.
systems.availability_note: Public research source with environment-specific pipelines; not installed or run.
systems.requirements: Python dependencies, model access, Mind2Web data or WebArena environments, and the documented filtering assets.

systems.name: agent-qa
systems.relationship_note: Standalone QA application documented by its maintainers. No relationship to an existing paper in this collection was established in this source review.
systems.learning_signal: Verified test-step evidence, later confirmations or contradictions, failure root causes, and user corrections to run verdicts.
systems.mechanism: After a run verdict is final, memidex derives candidate facts, cautions and reusable procedures from recorded evidence. A curator proposes record changes; deterministic checks and a promotion gate control which facts and cautions become active. Local runs apply eligible changes while CI retains proposals. Later tests receive relevant records in a brief and can reuse confirmed procedures.
capabilities: Plain-English web, Android and iOS testing through CLI and local MCP
Persistent memidex app knowledge with provenance and outcome logs
Evidence-checked learning with human correction and rollback
Optional replay and canary evaluation of candidate knowledge
systems.evaluation: Official documentation describes an optional corpus of reviewed recorded decisions. Canary comparisons start when the corpus exists; replay checks require a measured noise floor. Candidates are compared with and without their memory contribution, alongside evidence from later runs. This describes the project evaluation protocol, not independently reproduced performance.
systems.limitations: The documented improvement loop changes app knowledge rather than its own prompts or code; it is not evidence of recursive agent redesign or model training. CI does not automatically promote learned records. Parts of the online documentation label search and cross-workspace limits as v0.2: semantic retrieval depends on local model availability, and learned knowledge serving depends on local indexes and evidence. Release-to-documentation correspondence and runtime behavior were not audited.
systems.availability_note: Public repository, npm package and official documentation inspected as sources. No package was installed and no agent-qa runtime, model call or benchmark was executed for this collection.
systems.license: FSL-1.1-ALv2; Apache-2.0 future license after two years for each version
systems.requirements: Node.js 24 or newer, a configured compatible model endpoint or supported subscription workflow, and the relevant browser or mobile test environment. Docker is required only for tests using hooks. Model/API and execution infrastructure costs are separate.

systems.name: Agent0
systems.relationship_note: The official repository now hosts the Agent0 series, including a separate vision-language project. This entry describes the Agent0 language-agent subdirectory linked to the cataloged paper.
systems.learning_signal: Curriculum rewards, tool interactions, and self-consistency-filtered executor training data.
systems.mechanism: Alternates curriculum generation, task filtering, and reinforcement-learning updates of a tool-using executor. A deployed code sandbox supplies execution for multi-turn training trajectories.
capabilities: Train an executor through multi-turn RL
systems.evaluation: The paper and repository report reasoning benchmarks for particular trained models. This catalog did not run training or evaluate a released checkpoint.
systems.limitations: Zero data excludes new human-curated task labels, not pretrained weights, reward design, or tools. The documented workflow includes manual checkpoint selection between iterations.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Training-capable hardware, the documented veRL-based environment, pretrained model weights, and a configured SandboxFusion service.

systems.name: Darwin Gödel Machine
systems.relationship_note: Official DGM research code, with separate SWE-bench and Polyglot evaluation components and linked experiment logs; current source was not matched to a paper-run commit.
systems.learning_signal: Coding-benchmark outcomes and logs from candidate agent variants.
systems.mechanism: Runs a coding agent on changes to its own implementation and retains evaluated variants in an archive. Later iterations can build on earlier variants rather than only the most recent agent.
capabilities: Generate and evaluate self-edits to agent code
Maintain an archive of candidate agents
Inspect SWE-bench and Polyglot experiment artifacts
systems.evaluation: The related paper reports coding evaluations and ablations; the repository exposes the research loop and experiment logs. No result was independently reproduced here.
systems.limitations: The outer selection/evaluation process and foundation models remain fixed in the inspected study. The repository executes generated code and is a research implementation, not a validated general deployment service.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Python dependencies, Docker, configured model access, and benchmark environment/data preparation.

systems.name: DSPy
systems.relationship_note: Official DSPy framework; the original paper and GEPA describe particular optimization methods, not every capability of the current release.
systems.learning_signal: Developer-supplied examples and metrics, with feedback or fine-tuning objectives determined by the chosen optimizer.
systems.mechanism: Builds language-model applications from typed signatures and composable Python modules. Optimizers can produce reusable prompts, demonstrations, or tuned model parameters for a supplied task and metric.
capabilities: Compose reasoning, retrieval, and tool-using modules
Optimize instructions and demonstrations against a metric
systems.evaluation: The linked papers report evaluations of specific optimizers; current framework documentation supplies further application examples. This catalog does not test the latest release.
systems.limitations: Optimization must be configured with appropriate data, metrics, and models. A compiled program does not by itself become a continuously self-learning deployed agent.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Python 3.10 or newer, a supported language-model backend, and task examples plus an evaluation metric for optimization.

systems.name: EvoAgentX
systems.relationship_note: Official framework for the EvoAgentX paper; the old EvoAgentX/EvoAgentX URL redirects to ANative-Lab. Current modules can differ from the evaluated paper version.
systems.learning_signal: Task-specific evaluator feedback used by integrated workflow and prompt optimizers.
systems.mechanism: Combines workflow generation, execution, tool integration, and configurable optimization algorithms. Developers can retain optimized workflow definitions and add task-specific evaluators or operators.
capabilities: Generate, save, load, and run agent workflows
Integrate tools and human review points
Apply integrated prompt and workflow optimization
systems.evaluation: The associated paper reports benchmark comparisons; the repository describes an extensible software framework. Neither its feature list nor this inspection reproduces those comparisons.
systems.limitations: Automatic workflow construction is distinct from demonstrated continual learning. Optimizer integrations, task evaluators, and model/tool configurations still determine what can improve.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.license: MIT; bundled MIT notices are included in LICENSE
systems.requirements: Python environment and configured model backend; individual tools can require additional services or execution environments.

systems.name: Exo self-evolution experiment
systems.relationship_note: Research implementation at the paper-cited c5c1963 snapshot. Current official docs identify the self-evolving harness as an earlier experiment; the current default branch is not assumed to reproduce that snapshot.
systems.learning_signal: Task observations, retained execution history, failures, and recorded model usage guide self-edits.
systems.mechanism: The inspected research snapshot exposes harness source and runtime history to the agent and documents rebuild/restart, retained state, and sandbox recovery. Edits can change subsequent execution and later tasks.
capabilities: Inspect and revise harness source during tasks
Retain conversation and tool-event history across ordinary restarts
Rebuild executors and restore sandbox snapshots
systems.evaluation: The related paper reports game, application, service-incident, and coding evaluations. Source and documentation were inspected; no experiment was reproduced.
systems.limitations: The paper’s default guardian tests build success only. Broad development write access does not enforce its protection assumptions, and snapshots cannot reverse external effects. Current hosting documentation is under construction and covers a changed architecture.
systems.availability_note: Public pinned source, README, and license inspected. No installation, service launch, model call, or research-code execution.
systems.requirements: The research snapshot documents Git, Docker, Node/pnpm and Rust toolchains via mise, plus a supported OpenAI or OpenRouter model endpoint. Current setup documentation differs.

systems.name: ExpeL
systems.relationship_note: Official ExpeL implementation; repository availability does not establish reproduction of the paper scores.
systems.learning_signal: Training-task trajectories, success/failure comparisons, and extracted textual insights.
systems.mechanism: Collects agent experiences, extracts reusable natural-language lessons, and retrieves lessons and past examples during later inference. The learned state is external to the model weights.
systems.evaluation: The repository supplies configurations for HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, and WebShop and links the reported study.
systems.limitations: Experience quality and environment feedback shape the extracted insights. Environment setup and current API compatibility were not tested.
systems.availability_note: Public research code with train, insight-extraction, and evaluation entry points; not run.
systems.requirements: Documented Python 3.9 environment, model access, task data, and separate ALFWorld/WebShop setup when used.

systems.name: GEPA
systems.relationship_note: Official GEPA implementation; the current optimize_anything interface broadens the text-artifact optimization scope beyond the paper’s core prompt experiments.
systems.learning_signal: User-defined evaluation scores and diagnostic traces interpreted by a reflection model.
systems.mechanism: Uses reflection over execution feedback to propose textual edits and maintain a population of complementary candidates. Adapters connect the optimizer to prompts, program code, and other text-configured systems.
capabilities: Optimize prompts through DSPy or direct adapters
Track budgets, candidate history, and Pareto-based selection
systems.evaluation: The paper evaluates selected tasks and budgets; project documentation also presents demonstrations and use cases that should be assessed on their own protocols.
systems.limitations: The evaluator and search objective are externally supplied. Wider product examples do not establish the original paper’s results for every adapter or prove autonomous deployment learning.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: A Python environment, a reflection-model backend, an executable evaluation function, and examples or evaluation cases.

systems.name: Hermes Agent
systems.relationship_note: Upstream Hermes application. PAST-Bench studies a Hermes baseline and an experimental Hermes+ variant; this entry is not that benchmark modification or a claim of version equivalence.
systems.learning_signal: Completed task experience, user interaction, periodic memory prompts, and subsequent skill use.
systems.mechanism: Documents a persistent agent loop that creates and revises skills, maintains memory, and searches past sessions. Saved skills and memories remain available across later conversations.
systems.evaluation: Project documentation describes the learning loop; PAST-Bench provides a separate, bounded evaluation of selected Hermes configurations.
systems.limitations: Project feature claims do not establish indefinite improvement or perfect recall. Actual behavior depends on model, settings, task stream, and the inspected version.
systems.availability_note: Public application source with installers and desktop options; not installed or run.
systems.requirements: A supported local/hosted runtime and model-provider connection; optional cloud services have separate costs and terms.

systems.name: HyperAgents
systems.relationship_note: Official HyperAgents implementation accompanying the Hyperagents paper; task-agent and meta-agent code are separate editable components in the released research setup.
systems.learning_signal: Task evaluation and the histories of earlier agent modifications.
systems.mechanism: Makes both a task-solving agent and its improvement procedure editable. A fixed outer loop runs candidate changes and evaluation across configured domains.
capabilities: Inspect released experiment logs and analysis tools
systems.evaluation: The paper reports bounded multi-domain and meta-agent transfer experiments. The repository links experiment logs; no log-level audit or evolution run was performed.
systems.limitations: The outer task/evaluation boundary remains externally specified; this is not evidence of unconstrained improvement. The source is distributed under a noncommercial share-alike license.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Documented Python 3.12 and native build dependencies, Docker, model access, and the chosen domain environment.

systems.name: LangMem
systems.relationship_note: Standalone official memory/optimization library; no matching research paper is asserted in this catalog.
systems.learning_signal: Conversation histories, feedback, and extraction/consolidation prompts.
systems.mechanism: Supplies primitives for storing and consolidating agent experience, plus prompt-refinement tools. Applications can invoke memory operations during interaction or in background processing.
systems.evaluation: The inspected sources provide API examples and integration guidance, not an independently reviewed learning benchmark.
systems.limitations: The quickstart’s in-process store loses data on restart; durable retention requires a database-backed store. Library support alone does not establish a successful learning policy.
systems.availability_note: Public Python package and documentation; not installed or run.
systems.requirements: A supported model provider and storage backend; LangGraph integration is supplied, while functional primitives can use other storage.

systems.name: Letta Code
systems.relationship_note: Current Letta source, succeeding the MemGPT/Letta lineage; the historical letta repository identifies its V1 server as retired. Current behavior is not equivalent to the original MemGPT study.
systems.learning_signal: Conversation experience, explicit user lessons, background reflection, and agent-authored updates.
systems.mechanism: Maintains editable, git-backed memory and agent-scoped skills across conversations. Its documented mods mechanism can extend runtime behavior through locally trusted code.
systems.evaluation: The inspected official material documents mechanisms and user workflows; no learning benchmark of this current harness was independently assessed.
systems.limitations: Persistent edits do not guarantee improved task performance. Mods execute with the runtime’s trust and permissions, and features depend on configuration and host support.
systems.availability_note: Public application/harness source with npm and Python installation routes; not installed or run.
systems.requirements: A supported Node.js or packaged Python installation and configured model access; local, self-hosted, and cloud modes have different requirements.

systems.name: Mem0
systems.relationship_note: Official Mem0 software repository. The current managed-platform algorithm and SDK should not be assumed identical to the earlier paper implementation.
systems.learning_signal: User/agent conversation content and retrieved factual context.
systems.mechanism: Provides memory storage and retrieval for user, session, and agent context through libraries and a server. The managed platform adds functionality beyond the public SDK.
systems.evaluation: The current README explicitly attributes its headline benchmark scores to the managed platform, including proprietary optimizations.
systems.limitations: Those scores cannot be assigned to the open-source SDK unchanged. Factual recall and personalization do not alone establish procedural agent self-improvement.
systems.availability_note: Public SDK/server source and package instructions; hosted service is separate; nothing was installed or run.
systems.requirements: Library dependencies and configured model/embedding/storage backends; the server path uses Docker, while cloud use needs service access.

systems.name: MemRL
systems.relationship_note: Official implementation of MemRL with benchmark entry points; this is not model-weight reinforcement learning.
systems.learning_signal: Environment outcome feedback used to update episodic-memory utility estimates.
systems.mechanism: Combines semantic retrieval with learned utility values on episodic memories while keeping the reasoning model fixed. Useful experience can therefore influence later retrieval without parameter updates.
systems.evaluation: The README documents HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, and Lifelong Agent Bench evaluation entry points.
systems.limitations: Updating memory utility does not establish that the base model learned new capabilities. Feedback quality and retrieval settings remain part of the evaluated system.
systems.availability_note: Public Python research package with configurations and runners; not installed or run.
systems.requirements: Documented Python 3.10 setup, language-model and embedding endpoints, plus the chosen benchmark assets.

systems.name: ReasoningBank
systems.relationship_note: Official software release for ReasoningBank; supplied task integrations are distinct from a general production agent.
systems.learning_signal: Successful and failed trajectories assessed by model-based correctness judgments.
systems.mechanism: Extracts reasoning lessons from agent trajectories and retrieves them for subsequent tasks. Memory-aware test-time scaling supplies additional experiences for consolidation.
systems.evaluation: The release documents the software-engineering and web-browsing settings used by the paper.
systems.limitations: The agent judges its own trajectories in parts of the workflow. Current default-branch code and provider configurations were not independently reproduced.
systems.availability_note: Public research source with task-specific agent and evaluation directories; not run.
systems.requirements: Python dependencies, supported model-provider access, and benchmark environments; WebArena setup includes BrowserGym and Docker.

systems.name: SEAL
systems.relationship_note: Official Self-Adapting Language Models code, with separate general-knowledge and few-shot study directories; it is an adaptation research framework rather than a general agent application.
systems.learning_signal: Performance measured after applying a generated self-edit to model parameters.
systems.mechanism: Trains a model to generate adaptation data or update directives, then evaluates the gradient-based adaptation produced by those edits. The knowledge-incorporation implementation uses temporary LoRA training and evaluation to score candidate edits.
systems.evaluation: The paper reports knowledge and ARC adaptation studies, including retention tests. The repository contains code, data, and study documentation; these were not executed here.
systems.limitations: The related study still observes forgetting, and evaluating edits involves actual model training. The release should not be treated as a stable lifelong-learning service.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Python 3.12 and training dependencies; the README describes experiments using two A100/H100 GPUs and requires adapting provided SLURM directives to the execution environment.

systems.name: Self-Improving Coding Agent (SICA)
systems.relationship_note: Official experiment code for A Self-Improving Coding Agent; current repository behavior was not independently matched to the exact paper evaluation revision.
systems.learning_signal: Configured benchmark scores and archived results from preceding agent versions.
systems.mechanism: Alternates evaluating a coding agent, storing its results, and asking it to improve its own codebase. The next iteration uses the modified implementation.
capabilities: Inspect event traces in a local execution viewer
systems.evaluation: The paper reports selected coding and synthetic-task experiments; the repository provides loop configuration and trace inspection. No benchmark was run for this catalog.
systems.limitations: The repository recommends its Docker environment because the agent can run shell commands. It also identifies run variance and benchmark realism as open work; gains need not transfer beyond the selected tasks.
systems.availability_note: Public source and setup documentation inspected; not installed, trained, or executed for this collection.
systems.requirements: Docker, local Python dependencies, a configured supported model provider, and chosen benchmark resources.

systems.name: SkillRL
systems.relationship_note: Official training code and linked checkpoints for SkillRL; repository licensing does not determine every linked model or dataset license.
systems.learning_signal: Successful/failed trajectories, distillation data, and validation failures during reinforcement learning.
systems.mechanism: Distills experience into a hierarchical SkillBank and trains an agent policy with retrieved skills. Skill updates and model-parameter learning occur together in the training workflow.
systems.evaluation: The repository links SFT/RL checkpoints and documents ALFWorld, WebShop, and search training paths.
systems.limitations: This is a training stack, not a training-free memory plug-in. Checkpoint availability and source inspection do not reproduce the reported comparisons.
systems.availability_note: Public training source; model and dataset links are provided by the maintainers but were not downloaded.
systems.requirements: GPU-capable training setup with the documented vLLM/FlashAttention stack, task environments, model checkpoints, and configured provider access.

systems.name: Voyager
systems.relationship_note: Official research implementation of Voyager; the current checkout was not matched to a paper experiment commit.
systems.learning_signal: Minecraft observations, execution errors, and model-based task verification.
systems.mechanism: Explores Minecraft with an automatic curriculum and accumulates executable skills. Retrieved skills and iterative program repair support later tasks without fine-tuning the language model.
systems.evaluation: The README reports exploration and new-world skill-reuse experiments from the associated study.
systems.limitations: The environment uses Minecraft and supplied control APIs. Model-based verification and retained programs are not guaranteed correct; no experiment was reproduced here.
systems.availability_note: Public research source with setup instructions and a skill library; not installed or run.
systems.requirements: Python 3.9+, Node.js 16.13+, Minecraft with the documented mods, and a supported model API configuration.

routes.title: Foundations and boundaries
routes.question: What is the difference between solving a task and learning something reusable?

steps.why: Identify the fixed reasoning/action loop and its observations.
See how an answer can improve while the agent itself stays unchanged.
Trace how verbal feedback affects retries, and ask what survives a new task.
Follow the transition from individual trajectories to reusable cross-task insights.
Compare declarative insights with an executable skill library.
Place the mechanisms in a broader what/when/how taxonomy.

routes.exercise: Draw two timelines: one for a single task and one spanning several tasks. Mark every state update and every reset.

routes.title: Memory and skills
routes.question: How can experience become useful knowledge, a procedure, or a reusable tool?

steps.why: Start with extracting and reusing experience across tasks.
Follow workflow induction from successful trajectories.
Compare reusable reasoning memories extracted from successes and failures.
Separate learning a memory utility estimate from updating the reasoning model.
Compare memory-utility scoring with learning when to retrieve, distill, or skip experience.
Compare external experience routing with learned factual adapters; inspect forgetting, fallback retrieval, and write cost.
Contrast external skills with parameter learning and teacher-derived supervision.
Examine whether skill use produces measurable benefit.
Separate retaining a skill from keeping it selectable as the library grows; compare routing with task success.

routes.exercise: For three methods, write the stored artifact, admission rule, retrieval rule, revision rule, and evidence that reuse helps.

routes.title: Agent design and optimization
routes.question: Which parts of an agent can be optimized, and who performs that optimization?

steps.why: Understand compiling a declarative language-model pipeline with reusable parameters.
Inspect evolution of prompts and mutation instructions.
Compare textual feedback with reward-only search.
Expand the search from prompts to agent implementation code.
Study search over workflow operators and evaluation-driven selection.
Contrast whole-prompt replacement with incremental context updates.

routes.exercise: Make an editable/fixed component table. Include proposer, search space, selector, evaluation set, and stopping rule.

routes.title: Learning in model weights
routes.question: Where does supervision come from when a model helps generate its own training data?

steps.why: Track answer checks, rationale generation, and fine-tuning.
Distinguish generated instruction coverage from verified correctness.
Examine the generation/filtering/learning cycle and its external reward signal.
Ask what changes when a model also supplies preference judgments.
Separate a learned correction policy from untrained prompting.
Study generated self-edits, adaptation rewards, and retention limits.
Distinguish label-free adaptation to test questions from transfer to unseen tasks, and agreement from correctness.
Compare persistent online adapter updates with external training and within-task retries.

routes.exercise: For each loop, label which information is human-provided, pretrained, environment-verified, or model-judged.

routes.title: Self-play and curricula
routes.question: Can a system generate useful challenges for itself?

steps.why: Start with a domain whose rules and outcomes provide exact feedback.
Move from game outcomes to executable reasoning tasks and proposer/solver roles.
Inspect a challenger/solver curriculum and its dependence on model-derived signals.
Study agent-generated tool-use challenges.
Compare curriculum and executor co-development under tool-related objectives.
Audit seed answers, external retrieval, and model verification in a search proposer–solver loop.
Examine self-evolution in search, where external information changes the feedback setting.

routes.exercise: Explain what “zero data” excludes for each method and what prior information or engineered environment remains.

routes.title: Improving the improver
routes.question: Does a method change only the solver, or also the process that improves it?

steps.why: Identify how generated program improvements can feed back into the improvement procedure.
Inspect self-referential program modification.
Study archive-based search and empirical selection of self-edits.
Trace which meta-agent components become editable and which outer controls remain fixed.
Compare runtime harness edits with the fixed mechanisms that retain history and activate replacements.
Inspect modular evolution and frozen downstream evaluation.
Test the assumption that an optimization benchmark is a trustworthy teacher.
Distinguish final-system gains from repeated loops and same-start comparisons of improvers.

routes.exercise: Draw the solver, proposer, selector, and evaluator separately. Highlight what can change and what evidence would demonstrate improvement of the improver.

routes.title: Evaluation and failure modes
routes.question: What experiment would convince you that an agent learned something useful?

steps.why: Begin with feedback and fair-comparison pitfalls.
Study matched retained-experience controls with fresh sessions.
Distinguish a stored lesson from causal use of that lesson.
Distinguish changed behavior, legal actions, useful decisions, and preservation when artifacts are combined.
Compare performance under different task-stream compositions.
Inspect training/test rule recombination and task-selection effects.
Measure a frozen null before interpreting per-problem changes.
Include integrity of the learning signal and persistence of bad updates.
Inspect statistical acceptance under noisy feedback and the limits of a per-candidate guarantee.

routes.exercise: Draft a matched frozen baseline, a held-out family split, a budget ledger, and one intervention that could falsify your preferred mechanism.

routes.title: Continual learning, retention, and drift
routes.question: Does learning persist when tasks and environments change?

steps.why: Inspect inter-task dependencies and the limits of replay.
Separate a proposed lifelong framework from its evaluated baseline protocol.
Study updates, temporal reasoning, and abstention in recalled information.
Test whether one domain’s experience helps or interferes with another.
Examine parameter adaptation and forgetting.
Connect forgetting to replay selection and conflicting action labels in continual robot learning.
Understand distributional loss under recursive replacement assumptions.
Compare replacement with accumulation, retaining the cost and assumption differences.
Extend retention questions to unsafe influence, repair, and resumed adaptation.
Test for interference and forgetting when memory, shared prompts, or harness files evolve.
Compare this small-subset harness study with the preceding held-out stream evaluation; trace conflicts in task-specific checks.

routes.exercise: Specify separate measures for factual memory, procedural transfer, backward retention, cost, and safety drift. Do not collapse them into one score.
